in writing. on 8 july 2015, i supported the report of the committee on employment and social affairs on the green jobs initiative, which the commission had already presented in july 2014. this document was part of the employment package and was based on the assumption that up to 20 million jobs could be created in the eu by 2020 through the so-called green economy. this report correctly accepts the definition of 'green jobs' developed by the international labour organisation, which refers to them as decent jobs that reduce emissions, reduce energy and raw material consumption, minimise waste and pollution, and protect and restore ecosystems. the proposal put forward by the green group and rapporteur jean lambert was strong, environmentally friendly and in favour of workers, and aimed to ensure that workers and their collectives were not left behind in the transition to a low-carbon or zero-carbon economy. the proposal calls for the targeted development and teaching of green technology skills to workers and students, including workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the suppression of the development of polluting industries. it states that the jobs created in the green economy must be of high quality and sustainable. since the subsequent negotiations managed to preserve the original strengths of the text, i decided to support this report.
in writing. green jobs, according to the international labour organisation, are decent jobs that reduce energy and raw material consumption, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, minimise waste and pollution, and protect and restore ecosystems. however, the european parliament has supported a broader concept of green employment and is considering it in the general context of greening the economy. green jobs seek to respond to the biggest challenges: inefficient use of resources, unsustainable pressures on the environment and climate change, as well as social exclusion and social inequality. i fully support the call for a coherent comprehensive policy framework to ensure a predictable environment for both training and investment. these include investing in energy efficiency and energy poverty, which are long-standing topics in my parliamentary work. for example, estimates of the impact of the energy performance of buildings directive on employment pointed to the creation of a possible two million jobs, many of which would not by their nature be transferred abroad. to support green jobs, further reform of the green tax, energy and resource efficiency and an industrial strategy to support investment in innovation in eu industrial policy are needed with the ambitious aim of making the eu the most resource-efficient economy in the world.
in writing. ‒ this initiative aims at supporting the much-needed shift to green growth and ensure europe maximises the job creation opportunities it brings. in the respect of eu competence in the employment sector, the eu should focus on boosting job creation through an appropriate use of existing eu funding. in order to bridge the skills gaps in europe by providing for instance necessary trainings, the eu should be able to foresee the changes in the job market. smes will need special attention in this respect: the combination of the green action plan for smes and an intelligent use of the new efsi programme should provide them with effective incentives and the appropriate framework to move to greener products and processes. during the votes i opposed references to ‘creating quality long-term jobs’ because the report already included provisions on ‘sustainable employment’.
in writing. ‒ while i do not want to challenge efforts to improve environmental and climate protection, i strongly oppose artificial efforts to green the economy, especially in the form of state interventions and subsidies, which do not lead to more economic growth but will mean more bureaucracy, controls, increased costs and ultimately a deterioration of the eu's competitiveness on world markets. artificial efforts to green the planet will also lead to a subsidy-based bubble. in the case of the czech republic, this is the case for example with solar power plants or biofuels, where there is even a conflict of interest where the dominant producer of biofuels is a company owned by a current member of the government that decides on the subsidy scheme.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on tax avoidance and tax evasion in developing countries. i was the shadow rapporteur of the econ opinion on this report. the final text includes the recommendations we defined for the economic side and it takes into account the specificities of developing countries. it is important to keep in mind that those countries do not have the same administrative and technical capacities as european countries to fight tax avoidance. that is why it is crucial that we give them a transitional period for the implementation of the oecd standard on automatic exchange of information. although developing countries do not always have the capacity to send the required information, it is of utmost important that they receive tax information from developed countries so that they can detect and correct abusive tax practices.
in writing. on 8 july 2015, i voted in favour of the report on tax avoidance and tax evasion, social protection and development in developing countries. tax havens and absolute bank secrecy, combined with zero taxation, always attract capital and income that should be taxed in other countries, creating harmful tax competition, undermining the fairness of tax systems, and affecting the environment in developing countries in particular. nor is the situation helped by tax evasion by companies that seek to avoid taxation by creating complex internal structures and by exploiting loopholes in tax laws. the report calls for an action plan to combat tax avoidance and evasion in developing countries. the report also urges the commission and the member states to assess the impact of european tax policies in developing countries and to eliminate practices that have a negative impact on developing countries. since many of our amendments were reflected in the compromises adopted, i decided to support the document.
in writing. ‒ tax evasion is always an important problem we need to tackle, but in this case especially for developing countries regarding their high illicit financial flow levels, high dependency on corporate taxation and low tax-to-gdp ratios. these countries are in most need of tax revenue for infrastructure, welfare, education and many other things, but struggle to achieve it, with a prevalence of the rich and powerful easily dodging tax payment. i am, therefore, rejoiced that this resolution is adopted by a clear vote. the eu must engage actively in supporting developing countries for a fair and efficient tax system with a transparent and responsible administration to eliminate exploitation of the existing loopholes. the fact that most global solutions at present are prioritising benefits on developed countries, or in many cases on the oecd countries, this must be balanced. hence i very much support the ambitious proposals in the report, among which country-by-country reporting, the creation of an inter-governmental body where developing countries participate equally in reforming the existing global tax system, and other things. in the light of the upcoming addis ababa conference, i look to further solutions that put tax justice into practice.
in writing. the report on tax evasion in developing countries is a very important subject, especially in the light of the forthcoming un conference in addis ababa, and deserves full support. it is not just about trying to increase and make tax collection more efficient, but also about the methods of achieving these goals in coordination with development aid. development aid has no single binding obligation in the eu, but after unification it could become a very important tool with a leverage effect on developing country governments, giving them a stronger incentive to enact effective and enforceable tax legislation. the human rights issue must not be neglected either. all development aid must be conditional on respect for universally recognised principles, such as the un universal declaration of human rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on tax avoidance and tax evasion in developing countries. it is essential that we support those countries in implementing the oecd standard on automatic exchange of information. it is of utmost important that they receive this tax information from more advanced countries so that they can detect and correct abusive tax practices.
in writing. ‒ i support the fight against tax havens and tax evasion in developing countries, because taxes should be paid where profits are made. however, the proposed report is unacceptable given the reference to the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base, which is a risky step towards a single eu tax policy, with the consequence of undermining tax competition within the eu and imposing huge taxation costs on businesses, especially smes.
in principle, i am in favour of the most modern and efficient waste management and resource use possible. but it does not appear that the european union or governments understand this issue better than the companies themselves, who themselves have incentives to be resource-efficient and resource-efficient. the eu cannot think that by limiting the use of resources it will contribute to a more efficient use of resources in the future.
in writing. i supported the circular economy report because i consider the circular economy to be an important building block of a sustainable economy and therefore an important and strategic area to be tackled head on rather than with our backs turned. europe can play a leading role in the world thanks to its technological advances, but only if it applies these technologies itself. i do not agree with the rejection of energy efficiency and waste management targets just because they would be difficult to achieve. i am convinced that reducing energy consumption and making more efficient use of resources is in the interests of greater economic stability and raw material price stability in europe. circular economy incentives can also be a catalyst for the development of new technologies and the creation of new jobs. clearly setting long-term objectives and sticking to them is the best way to unlock the potential in these areas and minimise the short-term costs of changing the economy to a more responsible and sustainable way of working.
‒ a circular economy is the ability to increase the productivity of resources by recycling and reusing them. i am glad that the strong text of the resolution was adopted, especially because of the significant contribution of the social democrats, who succeeded in putting a stronger tone into the text. i am convinced that a 30% increase in resource productivity by 2030 compared to 2014 is a realistic prospect and will lead to further growth and job creation in particular. to do this, it is necessary to set clear targets and indicators (e.g. a 2025 waste reduction target for municipal, industrial and commercial waste), revise ecodesign rules (life, repairability, reusability and recycling), renew the waste directive (new binding impact targets could lead to the creation of up to 180 000 new jobs) and adopt measures to decouple growth from the use of natural resources, which the social democrats have strongly advocated. i am pleased that the resolution also proposes specific recommendations, for example on the retail sector and its involvement in the distribution of unsold goods to charitable organisations. we need to realize the enormous potential of the term circular economy, and we need to go through a change in conservative thinking that often tells us to think of green and innovative things as expensive. the opposite is true, and i am glad that this view has prevailed in the european parliament.
in writing. i supported the report on moving towards a circular economy, as it is without doubt the only long-term sustainable path to future prosperity in europe. only organic production, waste management, recycling and consumption reduction can ensure a good environment for us and future generations. at the same time, however, these principles need to be implemented in a transparent and gradual manner to ensure that the eu remains competitive and that our legislation is clear and predictable to businesses.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament approved a report entitled ‘resource efficiency: moving towards a circular economy’. as an itre rapporteur for the opinion on the legislative part of the package i was personally very much interested in this file and i submitted several amendments on the report. i am glad that the european parliament approved the report by a comfortable majority and confirmed the importance of this issue. the report contains a number of recommendations on setting non-binding targets for energy efficiency, introducing common definitions and systems for waste sorting and waste management. it deals also with the production phase, supporting the emergence of the market for secondary raw materials and the energy efficiency of buildings. this report serves as an input for the european commission, as the commission will introduce a new, revised and more comprehensive package of measures for the transition to the circular economy by the end of 2015.
in writing. i couldn't support the report. i consider the requirement to introduce mandatory separate collection of biological waste by 2020 to be problematic, the deadline is very difficult to meet. this is similar to the binding targets for the reduction and total prohibition of landfilling, and the text also makes the conditions for the operation of incineration plants worse.
‒ the european atomic energy community (euratom) is a comprehensive and autonomous body which oversees all aspects of the functioning of the nuclear industry, including the establishment and enforcement of safety standards for the protection of human health. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the nuclear industry.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the creation of a capital markets union because i believe that there is a need to achieve greater efficiency in capital markets while creating a fairer and more economically sound link between risk and return in eu capital markets. i believe that before presenting the relevant legislative proposals, the commission should carry out a thorough analysis of the current state of capital markets by country and, in a comprehensive economic analysis, assess the areas where union-wide barriers to investment through capital markets exist, assess the extent of those barriers and indicate the means by which they could be removed or minimised. where an unlawful approach would suffice, this should be the way to go. emphasis should be placed on identifying and assessing cross-border risks in eu financial and capital markets arising from institutional, legal and regulatory differences between member states and on finding appropriate solutions to facilitate cross-border capital flows.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the com proposal for a european agenda on security. the text includes strong and balanced recommendations towards strengthening the european response to terrorism and the threats posed by foreign fighters and cyber-crime. the eu can bring added value in this area by helping member states to adopt a coordinated approach. one of the aims of this agenda is to make sure all actors involved in the fight against terrorism effectively cooperate and improve information exchanges when necessary. in this respect, the mandatory registration of persons suspected of terrorism in the schengen information system is a good approach.
in writing. i voted against because i do not agree with the eu's central intervention in the member states' power to determine their internal and external security policy. the resolution is also misleading in that it attempts to conflate security and social issues.
in writing. the motion for a resolution requires careful consideration and a few comments. the first concerns the misuse of the term 'radicalism' in the text, in a pejorative sense. you can't gamble with terms that have a wide range. i would welcome, for example, a radicalisation of the fight against corruption in the european union. also, the effort to prevent companies from escaping to tax havens would be more radical. furthermore, i fear that the radicalization of social and political movements fighting poverty through austerity measures or production cuts, for example through outsourcing, may not be prevented without suppressing human rights. the second point concerns terrorism and crime. i would point out that the proposal completely ignores the causes of the rising tide of terrorism and the danger of war, and i would point out the overlooked motive that is associated with this issue. and that's the sale of small arms and light weapons. it is still subject to insufficient international regulation. small arms and light weapons account for 60 to 90% of all conflict casualties. the weapons of terrorists and organized criminals are precisely these types of weapons. according to the geneva small arms survey, a number of union states are among the largest exporters of these weapons. including exports to markets and battlefields where control is lost. i couldn't support the text.
‒ we are at a time when threats to the internal security of the union are becoming more complex and unpredictable, with the result that any state is losing the capacity to fully address them. this includes in particular the issue of terrorism, violent extremism, cross-border organised crime and cybercrime. this therefore requires more than ever coordination at pan-european level with respect for the rule of law and fundamental rights. i consider the programme proposed by the commission for the period 2015-2020 to be a high-quality and comprehensive document, emphasising its expected flexibility and capacity to respond to future challenges. i believe that at a pan-european level we must first tackle the root causes of crime, such as inequality, poverty and discrimination, which are likely to be present all the time, but it is up to us to what extent. i am firmly of the view that more investment is needed in preventive policies, even if repressive measures are also necessary. the european union is not isolated from the rest of the world, and therefore there is a need for closer cooperation with third countries, both logically and at economic and social level. in the light of a number of past cases, i would like to refer to one of the priorities of the european parliament's position, namely to improve the democratic and judicial oversight of intelligence services of third countries. the boundaries between security requirements and the protection of personal data exist and must be respected.
i did not support today's motion for a resolution on the european agenda on security because its final version is more dangerous than safe. the issue of security must be taken very seriously today and it cannot be used for populist purposes, either by restricting personal freedoms in the name of security or by treating security bodies with a priori suspicion in the name of fundamental human rights, as the final text does. the supervision and control of the exercise of all the powers of the state is one of the main components of a democratic state and, in the present state of advanced technology, it is certainly a challenge to ensure proper supervision, especially of the activities of the security forces. i believe that the only solution is parliamentary oversight, because the chain of the various inspection bodies has to end somewhere, and parliament is the right place to do so.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution for a european agenda on security. the text includes strong and balanced recommendations towards strengthening the european response to terrorism and the threats posed by foreign fighters and cyber-crime. the eu can clearly make a difference in the fight against terrorism. cooperation between member states is a key tool in this respect.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as i am seriously concerned at the rapidly deteriorating political, security and humanitarian situation in yemen. yemen is on the brink of civil war. since the houthi rebels’ advancement into the capital sana’a in september 2014, houthi rebels have been exploiting the power vacuum and fighting has been ongoing. the first victims of this violence are the civilians and according to un humanitarian agency more than 150 000 people have been displaced. the fighting has destroyed, damaged or disrupted at least five hospitals, 15 schools, yemen’s three main airports, two bridges, two factories and four mosques, as well as markets, power stations and water and sanitation facilities, ocha said. furthermore, the consequences of instability in yemen extend far beyond its borders, with terrorist cells such as al-qaeda in the arabian peninsula and the islamic state thriving amongst the current chaotic environment. it is thus critical that the international community react to this situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report calling on the eu and its member states to address the root causes of the rapidly deteriorating situation across the mena region through a holistic and ambitious approach. today, one of the main concerns in the region is the terror perpetrated by isis. this is why i strongly support the international campaign against isil/daesh and welcome the commitment of the coalition partners to working together under a common strategy. but i also believe that there is no answer to the crisis in the region without a regional dialogue involving all regional stakeholders, in particular the las, saudi arabia, egypt, turkey and iran.
in writing. at first glance, the right contains a number of positive thoughts and proclamations. for example, the rapporteur proposes even, he says, with a view to tangible concrete improvements for citizens in partner countries to strengthen the social dimension of the european neighbourhood policy, to step up the fight against poverty, to stimulate employment, to support education. but he admits that there is a lack of money for these eu-wide blasphemous goals. nor can the document hide the union's 'devotion' to the new ukrainian leadership or the policy's helplessness towards the other countries included in the epc. i would like to remind you of libya, israel and palestine, syria. the document had to acknowledge that eu policy had failed, for example, to prevent 'the doubling of networks for trafficking in arms, drugs and people in africa, with the consequent threat to the stability of europe'. it's got a lot of fun challenges, but i don't think even the reporter knows how to do them. in a policy towards 'neighbours of neighbours', the report calls for the promotion of bilateral relations, the strengthening of cross-border cooperation, people-to-people contacts. do sanctions against russia and specific individuals, including the paralysis of the work of parliamentary delegations, which have been responsible for the development of cross-border cooperation between the russian kaliningrad region and poland, contribute to the fulfilment of these general findings? since there are far more examples of failure or weakness in the epp than positive signals for its future, i cannot support this report in the ep.
in writing. ‒ in march this year, the european commission called for a public consultation on the european neighbourhood policy, to which the european parliament's report responds. i consider the european neighbourhood policy to be a fundamental pillar of the eu's foreign policy and at the same time one of its greatest challenges. the eu must be much more ambitious in this area, as inconsistency or underestimation has led and can continue to lead to instability in the wider world. now we're seeing the consequences of that in the case of ukraine. our approach must be strategic, coherent, but also specific, precisely targeted and based on detailed knowledge of the specificities of the countries concerned. the text of the document we adopted calls for the establishment of a position of eu special representative for relations with the south-eastern neighbours, which would undoubtedly lead to the strengthening of this policy and allow the dimension of the neighbourhood policy to be taken into account permanently in the wider foreign policy context. the key dimension of the neighbourhood policy must be security. it must include crisis management tools and support for the security structures of our neighbours. an ambitious neighbourhood policy, which is linked first and foremost to our internal security, will not be without relevant financial resources, which will be the subject of debate in the context of the 2017 review of the eu's external financial instruments.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the review of european neighbourhood policy. indeed i believe in the importance and the necessity of the review of the enp. i also think that the revised enp should be able to provide a quick, flexible and adequate response to the situation on the ground, while also putting forward an ambitious strategic vision for developing relations with the neighbouring countries in both a bilateral and a multilateral framework.
in writing. - i supported this report because as the situation in neighbouring countries changes, so must our policy towards them. neighbouring countries are experiencing constant change, less stability and a deeper economic crisis due to an increasing number of long-term security challenges. partner countries should seek a peaceful solution to the current situation, in particular because conflicts are hampering the social, political and economic transformation of countries.
mr president, i would like to explain why i voted in favour of the resolution on the implementation of the directive on the harmonisation of copyright. the directive has generated interest because of the so-called freedom of panorama. this provision, which was incorporated in the draft report by the committee on legal affairs, was finally omitted in the vote. this would mean restrictions on taking photographs or videos and displaying them in public places. i think it was a proposal that was not thought through enough and would have upset the balance between the relationship of authors and consumers that we're looking for. i think that this report does contain important references to access to cultural heritage through online platforms, also in the context of the appeal to legislators to allow easier access to educational materials. that is why i think it was good that this report was supported.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the copyright reform report. there are a number of strong ideas in the report, but most attention has centred on the so-called ‘freedom of panorama’. the text as adopted by the juri committee took what i would describe as an illiberal approach to this question. the amendment tabled to the paragraph by colleagues did not, in my opinion, clearly represent the sentiment of the many citizens who have taken an interest in this issue, so i felt that a better approach would be to delete the paragraph in its entirety.
in writing. on 9 july 2015, we voted on the report on the implementation of the directive on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society, known by the media acronym 'freedom of panorama'. this news, unfortunately, has unleashed a huge media storm, completely without meaning. we all probably agree that it is absolutely essential that the law respond flexibly to developments in the world around us. it's not always like that. the issue of regulating undesirable behavior and protecting copyright on the internet is precisely the area where the law has long failed. it is very difficult to find common ground on how to respond to the latest developments. one of the main reasons is the existence of very different legal traditions in the legal systems of the different member states. the original text was a very ambitious proposal calling for greater harmonisation, the introduction of mandatory copyright exceptions and the introduction of a so-called single european copyright title. after complex and difficult negotiations, my colleagues have managed to negotiate compromise amendments which strike a balance between the protection of authors, users, citizens' rights of access to cultural goods and information, and the protection of local cultures and traditions, while not hampering the development of new technologies. since the plenary succeeded in getting the amendment on freedom of panorama removed, i decided to support the report.
in writing. i am fully aware of the importance of european copyright law. the european cultural industry has an annual turnover of around eur 540 billion and creates more than 7 million jobs across the eu. the debate on ms red's report was very complex from the outset. some are concerned about the fate of europe's cultural industry, which they see as being threatened by large global companies such as google. others point out that with the advance of digitization, it is time for copyright rules to change. i can agree with that, technology outpaces the law! however, after several months of intensive work, i have come to the conclusion that the eu is not currently ready for full harmonisation of copyright. this is due to the traditional historical differences in the arrangements between member states. after many meetings and bilateral discussions with the shadow rapporteurs, i believe that we have managed to find a balanced compromise across the political spectrum, one that guarantees a balance between the rights of artists, producers and users, while allowing everyone access to culture through copyright, which must serve society as a whole and not just commercial interests. in addition, because we were able to defend the freedom of panorama, which was a key factor for me in the vote, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. report on the implementation of directive 2001/29/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 22 may 2001 on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society i supported the omission of this point from the report and therefore the retention of the existing legislation which gives member states the choice of either enshrining the freedom of panorama in full in their legal systems or restricting it with the consent of the copyright holders. the debate, which was heated and sometimes hysterical, with myths prevailing over reality, would not have occurred if the rapporteur had stuck to her original task of limiting her report to an analysis of the implementation of the directive in force, rather than arbitrarily taking it as a concept for revising the eu copyright legislation, which is one of the most complex and sensitive areas of eu law in the face of the dynamic development of modern technology.
in writing. european artists undeniably deserve to be strengthened and their copyright better protected. but that does not change the fact that we cannot allow the rights of european citizens to be reduced in a literal and reckless manner at the expense of this. that is why i voted against the amendment tabled by mr cavada in the report on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society. as the media have reported extensively, this part of the report could have immense implications if it were to be followed in the future by the european commission. it is inconceivable that in an age of strong technological development, citizens' rights are restricted to such an extent that they simply cannot share the photographs they take in public spaces. not only could the adoption of this provision lead to restrictions on the dissemination of non-commercially produced images on social media, but it could also affect, for example, the growing trend of blogging or the use of online encyclopedias. although i support the wider use of electronic libraries to improve access to information or to limit the power of large corporations to the detriment of artists, which are some of the positive aspects that the report contained and for which i voted, i still have a bad taste in my mouth. the stench of the legal affairs committee allowing a citizen's depravity of such caliber to enter the plenary.
in writing. the copyright report by julie redová rightly raised concerns among the european public, including the czech public, in particular because of the paragraph proposing to restrict the so-called freedom of panorama. when the principle of freedom of panorama is applied, it means in practice that the person who records or expresses in any way (photographically, by drawing, film, etc.) a work placed in the public domain does not infringe copyright and does not need to obtain a licence. the right to panoramic views varies from one country to another, and the czech republic has a relatively high degree of freedom of panoramic views. while the problematic paragraph limited the purely commercial use of photographs, videos or other representations of works, its impact could have far wider consequences. i am therefore very pleased that, after internal discussions in the european parliament, within the political group and across the political spectrum, we have reached the decision to remove the proposed measure from the text and have adopted today a useful document that will serve as a basis for new commission legislative proposals. our goal for the future should be to improve copyright protection, but i consider and will always consider it unacceptable to make life unnecessarily complicated for ordinary internet users.
in writing. i decided to support this often misinterpreted proposal, since its aim is nothing less than to protect consumers and authors and to strengthen the single european market. copyright harmonisation will open up the entire european market to authors from different countries, make the same content available to all consumers and improve the competitiveness of european cultural production, which is essential for functioning in today's fast-changing technological world.
in writing. i supported the final version of this report because i believe that, although the initial text of the report in particular was somewhat out of date, the result was a balanced text that will allow us to continue the discussion on the reform of intellectual property rights in the european union in order to achieve a modern approach that respects the legitimate interests of creators, rightholders and users.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the initiative report on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights. with the digital single market, the european union is jumping into the digital era which, for the cultural industry, is a challenge as great as the opportunities it brings. therefore it is necessary to set out our intentions as regards the harmonisation of copyright across the eu, in prevision of a commission proposal. i supported the provisions recalling the necessity of addressing geo-blocking and ensuring the portability of rights, in respect of the freedom of movement on which the internal market is built: consumers should not be denied access to certain content based on their geographical location in the eu. i opposed the provision restricting the freedom of panorama because i believe one should be able to record images of a public landmark and use it as one wishes. public space is, by definition, public and its use should not be subject to any kind of authorisation. that is why i voted to delete the paragraph restricting the freedom of panorama.
in writing. ‒ i oppose the proposal to restrict the so-called freedom of panorama and i am convinced that the current regulation in czech legislation is sufficient and that there is no need to seek harmonisation within the european union. i am aware that some eu member states, such as france, belgium, greece and italy, have this freedom of panorama limited in some way, but the amendment of the directive should not change the current situation where member states decide this themselves.
in writing. on 9 july 2015, i voted against the report on the eu's new approach to human rights and democracy: an evaluation of the activities of the european foundation for democracy (efd) since its creation. i must say at the outset that i reject both the analyses of the eed's results and the very purpose of this organisation. i do not agree with the eed's activities, because they are based on the so-called democratisation regime, which means complete liberalisation/privatisation at the economic level. the most recent example of the eed's democracy-building efforts is the situation in ukraine. under the umbrella of 'democratization', the organisation's main objectives include funding various political parties. from my point of view, this is a clear interference in the internal politics of foreign, sovereign countries, the will to implement a political, economic and social system based exclusively on the majority right-wing capitalist system. i consider that both this organisation and the very objective of its neighbourhood policy violate the fundamental rules of public international law, since article 2.4 of the un charter already contains the principle of non-interference. i believe it is essential that we defend the right of all peoples to decide for themselves their future and their political, economic and social development. i only support a policy of cooperation based on equality and solidarity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this evaluation of activities of the european endowment for democracy. by voting for this report, i welcome the eed’s track record given the current challenging international environment. i also consider that it is fulfilling its main objective of ‘fostering and encouraging democratisation and deep and sustainable democracy in countries in political transition and in societies struggling for democratisation’. for the future, i believe that the eed should continue to develop new innovative means and instruments for democracy assistance, including for political actors or activists, and to share best practices in order to adjust to the growing climate of restriction in a number of countries with authoritarian regimes.
in writing. i consider the work of the european foundation for democracy to be very useful. the edf fulfils its core mission of promoting and fostering democracy, in particular by fighting corruption and violence and by fostering dialogue on the diversity of political orientations. the edf does its utmost to meet the recommendations of the european parliament, and i therefore rate its work very positively.
in writing. at the strasbourg plenary session on 9 july 2015, we also voted on a resolution on the current situation in burundi. i abstained from voting on this resolution. for several reasons, as set out below. the proposal not only lacked more precise data on the number of people who were forced to flee the country, but the vague figure of 127 000 burundian refugees is, according to official sources, far from accurate. unfortunately, there are many more who have gone missing. the motion should also, in my opinion, have stated that the burundi constitutional court has clearly stated that the text of the constitution states unequivocally that the president can only be elected for two terms. however, mr nkurunziza does not count his first presidential term, despite publicly promising not to exceed the constitutional limit of two terms. this should have been clearly stated in the report. the situation in burundi is currently very difficult and many points of the proposal itself have not been sufficiently developed. however, at least this report informs the european public about the current, alarming situation in burundi, yet there are still many missing pieces of information, the absence of which makes the report not present the current situation in a realistic and up-to-date way.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution calling for an immediate halt to violence, that urges the burundian authorities to postpone the presidential election and calls on all parties involved in the electoral process. the conflict in the country needs now to come to an end and i call on all parties to resume dialogue.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that the european parliament is joining in condemning the terrible crime committed in srebrenica two decades ago. to prevent similar crimes from being repeated, the context must also be kept in mind. the idea that the crimes of the civil war are committed by one side only, only causes pain and fuels hatred. we must not forget that the real crime was the war itself, which was taking place throughout the former yugoslavia. a war that has killed an estimated 140,000 people and made four million refugees. when we talk about the crimes of the serbs in bosnia and herzegovina, we must always remember that the blame lies with individuals, not with a nation. and let us also remember that the first ethnic cleansing of this terrible war was directed against the serbs in croatia. let me express my conviction that the horrors of the war in yugoslavia would not have occurred if the parties to the conflict had not been supported from abroad. and it wasn't just about diplomatic support. the balkans were flooded with foreign weapons during the war. this was done despite the embargo. there is still a lack of a truly expert and, above all, independent historical analysis of the nature of this war, even in this resolution, which is why i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on srebrenica to commemorate and honour all the victims of the srebrenica genocide and of all the atrocities during the wars in the former yugoslavia. by this vote i also wanted to express my condolences to and solidarity with the families of the victims.
on behalf of the alde group.– mr president, a strong civil society is vital to any democratic process. in congo, civil organisations have an exceptional role in filling the void of a state that fails to provide fully for its citizens. peaceful and civic engagement should never be punished. congo cannot silence the violence of its people or deny them the right to mobilise. the fact that recent violations have specifically targeted youth movements and the political opposition is additionally disturbing. as a first step towards reconciliation with its own people, yves makwambala, fred bauma and all arab political prisoners must be released. the congolese authorities should make use of the critical benefits brought by an active civil society. a dynamic civil society not only keeps the state in check but also brings the community the capacity to resolve common problems. it is time for the congolese authorities to celebrate this as a virtue rather than attack it as a threat.
in writing. it is symbolic that we are taking an interest in human rights in the democratic republic of congo today in brussels. i don't think i'm going to offend anyone by recalling some historical facts. according to the encyclopædia britannica, when the belgian king acquired the congo as a colony in 1885, it had a population of 20 million. in a quarter of a century, the population of the country has dropped to 8 million. i am reminded of this because belgium, as a constitutional monarchy, already had a model constitution with a noble declaration of human rights. how many years did it take for the ideals of human rights to apply to this colony? two world wars were fought before the republic of congo gained independence in 1960. today, too, many africans, especially in the former belgian congo, will no doubt look with contempt on european recommendations on human rights. but i don't think we should be discouraged. we just need to do more by example, less by pressure and less by mentoring. we must honor the traditions of the land and remember the greatness of men like patrice lumumba. and we also have to get rid of the illusion that a modern civil society can be built on the basis of poverty and illiteracy. we must help in these areas if we are not to pave the way for a new mobutu to come to power instead of perfecting democracy. human rights in developing countries cannot be dictated by domestic law or imposed by western armies.

the rapporteur. ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to present to you the report on promoting youth entrepreneurship through education and training. the report draws on a wealth of knowledge from education systems and the business environment and concludes with a clear conclusion: entrepreneurial skills are required, can be taught and can be learned. it's good for the individual and good for society. the report has been the subject of 225 amendments to the original report, which has generated a great deal of interest and is the result of very good cooperation with the rapporteurs of all the groups, to whom i also express my thanks. the european parliament's report is a response to the high level of youth unemployment, which in some regions is as high as 50%. the european union institutions have repeatedly paid attention to promoting young entrepreneurship. however, this report is the only one to deal with this subject in isolation. we agreed, among other things, that young people need to develop a sense of initiative and entrepreneurship. we emphasize the social dimension of business. our report highlights the role of non-formal and informal education, which is the domain of the non-profit sector in particular, and exceptionally of companies, and which needs to be recognised and promoted. the report deals in detail with the definition of entrepreneurial skills and the possibilities for teaching them. the european parliament affirms that 'a sense of initiative and entrepreneurship' is one of the key competences for lifelong learning. it includes, among others, creativity, the ability to innovate, to take risks, financial and media literacy, and to plan and manage projects. the report focuses on the role of the european commission and the council and calls for better use of the instruments they have. for the european commission, this resolution represents a major challenge. in view of the proactive approach taken by dg eac so far, we take the liberty of setting specific dates and tasks. for example, for the commission to strengthen the promotion of entrepreneurship education as one of the objectives of the erasmus+ programme for the next financial period after 2020 and for these skills to be included in the compulsory content of the training programmes. the european commission should include measures related to training in this area in the european semester evaluation indicators from 2016. it should then submit a report on best practices in this area by the end of 2017. we are aware that member states are not waiting for this resolution, but are already working on developing entrepreneurial skills themselves, albeit in a very diverse and insufficiently systematic way. the european parliament therefore identifies measures that can help them, such as start-ups, mentoring, facilitating access to loans, crowdfunding or partnerships between businesses and universities, support for business incubators and, above all, linking education with practice. the funding sources for these activities will be the european social fund, the youth employment initiative, the european union programme for employment and social innovation, erasmus for young entrepreneurs and others. as teachers play a key role, we call on member states to initiate improvements in their training already within the pedagogical curricula. the european parliament sees great potential in promoting youth entrepreneurship through education and we therefore ask the commission to present to parliament, by the end of this term, an evaluation report on the progress made in this area. i thank my colleagues once again for their cooperation and i believe that the measures we are proposing will help to improve the quality of education and improve employment. business is for profit. for the entrepreneur, for the individual, for the employee, and for society as a whole.

in writing. i supported the revision of the regulation on trade in seal products, as it aligns the legislation to the recommendations and binding wto decisions on trade in seal products. the text abolishes the existing exception on marine resource management, as these catches cannot be distinguished from commercial catches. the report also amends the proposal on the indigenous community exemption, in particular taking into account the right of inuit or other indigenous communities to self-determination. i consider important the provision referring to the right of citizens to be duly informed that seal products placed on the eu market and derived from hunts organised by inuit and other indigenous communities have a legal origin. in addition, if it is shown that the numbers of seals caught under the so-called inuit exemption correspond to commercial catches, it will be possible to limit the quantities of products derived from these catches that can be placed on the market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposed regulation on trade in seal products. this regulation intends to comply with wto recommendations as regards exceptions to the ban on trade in seal products. until now the eu authorised an exception as regards maritime resource management (mrm); such exception is no longer needed. the second exception concerns the trade in seals conducted by inuits: seal hunting is a long-term tradition and is still today essential for their community. in accordance with the right to self-determination and the indigenous peoples’ right to traditional life styles, such an exception may remain and these products may be placed on the eu market, provided animal welfare is respected and limits are set out on the number of seal products which can be put on the eu market.

in writing. i abstained on the moi/sommer report. the reason is that i do not agree with the tightening of the commission proposal, which the ep has agreed to. cloning is a concern, but it also offers possibilities that need to be explored in the laboratory. a firm and permanent ban significantly undermines this research, because a firm and unlimited ban undermines the interest in this research. the commission proposal seemed to me balanced and sufficient, since it limited itself to a temporary suspension of the use of cloning for food production purposes and to the placing on the market of live clones (animal clones). this interim ban was to be followed by a review based on the development of knowledge on cloning and the progress in the use of this technique in non-commercial applications. the prohibition should exclude cloning carried out in the framework of research for the conservation of rare breeds or endangered species and for the production of medicinal products and medical devices. i regret that the ep has taken a radical view of this problem and has decided not to take the sensible path.
in writing. i supported the draft report proposing to tighten up the commission's original proposals to stop animal cloning. the commission has proposed to suspend the use of the cloning technique in the eu for the commercial marketing of live cloned animals and embryos and the marketing of food products from cloned animals (meat, milk, etc.). parliament not only refused to clone animals but also called for a ban on the import of cloned animals, which was not included in the commission's original proposal, so that the commission offered only a half-solution. cloning is itself primarily an ethical problem. on the one hand, it allows more efficient work with high-quality animal pieces, on the other hand, it is shown to have a very negative impact on the donor and, in particular, the recipient of the cloned egg, in particular in the form of increased health problems and frequent high pain. the ep report proposes a ban on the production of germinal products (sperm, oocytes and embryos) from clones for the purpose of reproducing animals (offspring of clones) by traditional reproductive techniques, in addition to cloning animals. there is scientific evidence that cloning practices cause poor living conditions for farmed females and offspring of clones also in farmed fish and poultry, although less significantly than in mammals. the ep has therefore pushed for the amendment to apply the measure to all farmed animals, and not just cattle, pigs, sheep, goats and equidae, as proposed by the commission.

in writing. i supported the report on the procedures and practice of commissioners' hearings experience gained during the 2014 hearings, as i believe that it contains a sober assessment of the experience gained in the past year and suggests adjustments to future practice that can contribute to greater efficiency and clarity of the whole process. it should be said that the practice of hearing commissioner-designate is indeed only an established practice, not regulated by the treaties, and that it is therefore necessary to continuously evaluate and improve these customary rules. it is not a bureaucratic exercise, but a necessary and useful reflection.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims at improving the hearings of commissioners and the overall selection process. from my experience last september i am in favour of reducing the number of questions meps can ask to the commissioner-designate to ensure a more in-depth discussion. if there is no consensus on a candidate, an additional enquire should be conducted through written questions and if necessary through another hearing. the scope of the declaration of interests should also be broaden so that all commissioners-designate are free of any suspicion.
in writing. i supported the owninitiative report by mrs schaake on two main points. first, it calls for clarification of the norms and standards that private entities use to develop their systems. the report points out that in the digital domain, private actors play an increasingly important role in all spheres of social activity, but there are still no safeguards to prevent them from unduly restricting fundamental rights and freedoms. in addition, as private actors thus play a more active role in assessing the legality of content and in developing cybersecurity and surveillance systems, their activities may have a negative impact on human rights worldwide. second, the report did not hide the activities of the national security agency, which were exposed by edward snowden. the report notes, for example, that the nsa has accumulated a large number of so-called zero day exploits it security vulnerabilities that are not yet known to the public or to the vendor, which weaken encryption protocols and products and frustrate global efforts to improve it security. according to the report, the active mass surveillance of citizens and the spying on political leaders by the nsa for the active cooperation of some eu member states, revealed by edward snowden, have seriously undermined the credibility of eu human rights policy and weakened global confidence in the benefits of information and communication technologies.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution, which calls on the commission to take further action (§ 16, 38, 44 and others), to set up expert committees (§ 54) and even to set up a new fund (§ 8).
in writing. ‒ i am pleased by the results achieved by the parliament on the important issue of human rights. the vote on the human rights and technology report shows that the european union is committed the rights of privacy and access to technology for all. it has become a worrying trend in some countries that the government will monitor and track communications on a mass scale, without any regard for an individual's privacy. these activates operate on the outskirts of the law and can undermine the pillars of democracy. when we stand idly by and let the actions continue, we undermine our own credibility in regards to human rights. in addition, we need to promote and protect those who bring attention to these privacy concerns. whistle-blowers, journalists and those who defend human rights should have proper protections, so that they have the ability to call attention to injustice, without fear of retribution. the eu must promote unrestricted access to the internet, this includes countering the criminalization of encryption tools, censorship by passing tools, and privacy tools as a whole. the eu has long been a champion of human rights, and it is time that we include digital rights to the equation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report which tackles an important issue which is a growing concern: the human rights violations through technological systems. technological developments play an important role in enabling the expression of fundamental freedoms such as access to information, freedom of assembly or right to privacy. however, these same technologies may be misused and result in censorship or surveillance. the report puts forward a list of recommendations for the eu to improve its standards as regards the use and export of ict systems to third countries. in particular, the eu should better encrypt its communication, seek the extension of international protection for whistle-blowers, conduct a human right impact assessment on its own ict policies.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims at optimising the use of eu subsidies for the common agricultural policy. the cap spending scheme is particularly complex because of the diversity of farming scheme throughout the eu and may lead to burdensome control procedures. the cost of the controls on the implementation of the cap amounts to eur 4 billion. i think it is urgent to find the right balance between leading an effective financial control and imposing less administrative burden.
in writing. ‒ the common agricultural policy represents a key item in the union´s budget also because it absorbs an extraordinary part of it. nevertheless, it has been and continues to be a very complex and not transparent expenditure over which there is a little control that tends to be very costly. this of course leads to a very high error rates, as determined by the court of auditors, and invites fraudulent activities. we need to simplify the administrative burden to make the process less bureaucratic but at the same time we need ensure sufficient monitoring over the finances in this area. i therefore support this call for increased quality above quantity with regard to financial controls, which will not cut a significant part of the cap’s budget, in the form of the single audit scheme. the controls need be effective as to secure financial interests of the european tax payers and need to be less burdensome and costly for the very same reason. i also believe that the member states should take responsibility for quality on-the-spot controls that are crucial for ensuring the correct usage of the european budget.
in writing. on 8 september 2015, i supported the report on family businesses in europe in the plenary session in strasbourg. 85% of all european businesses are so-called family businesses, which today also generate more than 60% of private sector jobs. the huge differences in the typology and structure of these bodies across the eu justify the need for new legislation by the european institutions. most family businesses have special relationships with both the territory in which they operate and their employees. however, it should be borne in mind that not all family businesses always show the positive effects mentioned above. some family businesses today rival the world's largest corporations. the text of the report calls for the promotion of this type of business through soft law, and i therefore believe that the report could have a positive impact on this type of business. unfortunately, the report lacks a proper definition of a family business which would exclude large family businesses (corporate size) as beneficiaries of these support measures.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i am fundamentally opposed to the eu adopting any legislation on family businesses, to the eu adopting binding definitions of family businesses and to pointless, wasteful programmes such as 'erasmus for young entrepreneurs'.
in writing. i supported the report on family businesses in europe, which have a significantly higher equity ratio than other businesses, and it is this high equity ratio that often ensures the economic stability of the business and the stability of the economy as a whole, while leaving the possibility for further investment in the business. i think it is a useful idea to create a single point of contact for businesses that could act as a contact body for family businesses, especially in relation to specific issues related to european legislation and access to eu funds. on the contrary, i consider it superfluous to set up a permanent working group within the commission services to carry out administrative reporting.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased by parliament’s vote on the family businesses in europe report. family businesses are a cornerstone to the eu’s vast economy. they are the single biggest source of employment in the private sector, and have played an enormous role in renewal and growth in the european economy as a whole. in addition, they provide good paying jobs to europeans across the region and play an important role in encouraging minorities and under-represented groups to participate in local economies. to help support this integral part of the economy, i would like to call on member states and the commission to help develop digital entrepreneurship and skills so that family businesses can take complete advantage of emerging and online technologies. i would also urge the commission to analyse the current legislation which affects family businesses to identify any issues and barriers to growth and success. family businesses play a crucial role in our economy, and we should do everything in our power to help them thrive.
in writing. i supported the report on family businesses in europe because i agree with the assessment of the role of family businesses on which this report is based. family businesses are an important part of the economy of each member state. family businesses focus on the long-term success of their businesses, providing much-needed stability in the labour market and contributing to well-functioning local communities. these qualities of family businesses should be recognised and efforts made to improve the conditions for their business so as to ensure their long-term survival even if a new generation of owners takes over. this is not an infringement of the competences of the member states, but a matter of concern whose solution will certainly benefit the citizens of all member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on family business in europe. creation of good conditions for business is one of my key agendas and i hope this report will contribute to this aim. furthermore, there are certain specifics of family business which should be taken into account while creating a new legislation or rules for business in general.
in writing. ‒ i support this report, which calls for simplification of legislation for family businesses so that they can develop their activities and cooperation in other member states without unnecessary administrative obstacles. family businesses are an important part of every national economy, as well as the european economy. these small enterprises are the ones that provide a large number of jobs and, moreover, have a high level of responsibility towards their own employees.

in writing. on 8 september 2015, at the plenary session in strasbourg, we voted on the report by my colleague from the group of the european people's party and the envi committee, lynn boylan, on the european citizens' initiative 'right2water'. the vote was very exciting this time. it was not clear until the last moment whether our report would be accepted by the full european parliament, as the people's party and the conservative party decided to put forward a completely different proposal. the european citizens' initiative is an important instrument of participatory democracy in the eu. this tool allows one million eu citizens residing in at least one quarter of the member states to call on the commission to propose legislation that they consider necessary to implement the eu treaties. given the way the commission is currently handling these citizens' initiatives, it was imperative that at least the european parliament would express support for eu citizens and take a strong line against the inaction of the commission. despite the nerve-wracking voting process, i can finally say that a good thing has happened. my colleague boylan succeeded and printed the report in almost the original form. in other words, qualifying the right to clean drinking water as one of the fundamental human rights and strongly rejecting any attempt to privatize free access to drinking water. i'm very glad i could support such a text.

madam president, i would like to explain why i did not vote for the report by mrs keller. not that i'm against solidarity. on the contrary, i did. it is necessary, necessary. it's an expression of our humanity. i try to help refugees with my own resources, especially christian families who come to the czech republic and are cared for. they're fleeing the persecution of the islamic state. and it's consistent with our values to help these people. i did not vote for the report, however, because it goes beyond the joint agreement of the member states on a one-off measure in the form of the relocation of 40 000 refugees, which was reached at the council meeting in june this year. i consider it essential that it is the representatives of the member states who are responsible for security who agree to accept refugees in their countries. the european parliament's role is certainly not to decide for them.

in writing. ‒ every member state has a moral duty to help the refugees arriving from conflict areas like syria or other war zones. we should help those who ask for our help. but i cannot support the mandatory introduction of quotas. if a refugee does not want to stay in one member state, we should not attempt to force them to. such a system would not work without the suspension of the schengen agreement and the freedom of movement that is fundamental to europe today. it is normal that a refugee will continue to move towards their preferred objective, where they might already have family or work, and no quota will stop this desire. each member states must be able to decide itself how many refugees to accept in its territory and accept those who truly desire their help. therefore, i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ as i share the views of the czech government on migration, i could not support the report on the draft council decision establishing temporary measures in the field of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece. it was again a question of quotas for the reception of refugees, with which i cannot agree. although i sympathize with the suffering of syrian refugees in particular, i consider forced solidarity to be a misunderstanding of the very meaning of solidarity, which must be voluntary. moreover, the absolute minimum of current refugees want to live in the czech republic, and i cannot imagine how we would keep them in our country by force in the 21st century. in addition, the czech republic has already given a home to refugees from many eastern countries, especially those fleeing civil war-torn ukraine. now, however, it seems that all the eu institutions have chosen to ignore this. the eu must realise that its only hope is to end the conflicts that have been the catalyst for today's events as quickly as possible. not all refugees want to stay in europe. they want to go home, but they're gonna risk their lives tonight. the solution is not quotas or the hate speech of ambitious political newcomers or aging matadors. the solution to the whole problem lies where the problem began, in north africa and the middle east.
in writing. i voted against it. i don't agree with mandatory quotas for the distribution of immigrants. i do not agree with the provision that 'member states [...] should agree on binding quotas' for the distribution of immigrants. i do not agree with the pressure for 'common european standards' for the reception of asylum seekers.
in writing. i supported the european parliament's position on the temporary international protection measures for the benefit of italy and greece. i did so despite the fact that some of the principles on which the proposed part of the solution to the immigration crisis is based are not, in my opinion, the most appropriate. i voted in favour because there is no other solution on the table and to oppose the commission's proposal in the absence of another option is to escalate the current crisis. a crisis that is not about an abstract problem, but about tens of thousands of specific people. i don't think the mandatory quota system is the best, although unlike many politicians i think it can be set up to work. because even refugees have to follow the rules. i would welcome an agreement among member countries on how to deal with the problem fairly and together. unfortunately, the past months have shown that the governments of the member states are not capable of such an agreement. the european parliament has therefore supported the opinion of the ep, as have 498 of my colleagues, because in a situation where 100 states do not agree to take on voluntary joint responsibility, the mandatory mechanism is the only solution that is really on the table, and in this sense also the only possible one.
in writing. - i voted against this report. the rejection of the proposed administrative mechanism, to be followed by a permanent system of redistribution of refugees among eu member states, should not be interpreted as a rejection of interpersonal solidarity and assistance to people in need. i believe that all member states and their citizens are ready for it. at the same time, and first and foremost, i call for the eu to make the maximum international diplomatic effort to end the war in syria and other conflicts in the eu's neighbourhood, which have already killed hundreds of thousands of people and are driving people from their homes, including to eu countries.
in writing. ‒ together with almost 500 democratically elected representatives of european voters, i voted in favour of the proposed recommendation to the council on the temporary relocation of refugees from italy and greece. i've waited a long time for our government to accept refugees voluntarily. she didn't do it, guided by the vision of the votes in the election. to show such a blatant and showy reluctance to show any sign of solidarity within the eu at a time of such a complex geopolitical situation, when europe must stand together, is a great gamble. the government has clearly prioritized electoral preferences over responsibility and also over simple humanity to the refugees. because it's refugees, people fleeing war, that we're talking about, not economic migrants. just to clarify, the ep does not co-decide in this case, but merely gives the council its opinion, which is not binding on the council, i.e. the member states.
in writing. i did not support the report on temporary measures in the area of international protection for the benefit of italy and greece, to confirm my previous opposition to the solution of the migration crisis through quotas. the migration crisis is a complex problem that has no simple solution. however, this solution or solutions to the individual but interrelated problems must be sought together at union level and must be actively involved in the discussion. in particular, our task remains to contribute to the future debate on the shape of eu asylum and migration policy. a system must be found to minimise the emergence of crisis situations and to resolve any crisis arising from causes beyond the eu or member states' competence quickly, efficiently and in compliance with humanitarian commitments that cannot be waived.
in writing. ‒ i did not vote in favour of this report as it only proposes short-term measures rather than providing a comprehensive approach to this complex problem. i could not particularly support the commission’s proposal to redistribute asylum seeker according to the mandatory quotas to the member states, which would force the asylum seekers to stay involuntarily in given countries.
mr president, i would like to say that i was pleased to support this report, which also discussed whether the eu institutions have the power or the competence to speak about urban mobility, about the urban agenda. i think that the debate is very late, or that it is really not appropriate to debate whether the urban agenda is within the scope of the european union. i'm sure you do. there is no doubt that the mobility trends of europe's population are converging in cities. that cities will be the home of the majority of the continent's population, and if the european union were to give up on the urban agenda, on urban mobility, it would undoubtedly give up on one of the main issues that is going to define the next period. i therefore hope that even colleagues who, in my view, inexplicably did not support this report will change their decision-making and thinking on this matter in the future, because the urban agenda, urban mobility, is a matter of eu policy and i was honoured to support this report.
‒ the european union is not about the future of cities. it will develop according to natural development and also to the demands of the inhabitants. urban development should therefore be left to the lowest level of decision-making.
in writing. ‒ i supported a report on the current and future challenges facing urban policy. as the current trend is for more people to live in cities, it is important to address today the questions of what cities people want to live in should look like in the future. important topics include sustainable transport, housing policy and energy networks. i agree with the argument that the eu's urban agenda should focus on the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and in particular on the themes of 'social inclusion, demographic change and sustainability'.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the urban dimension of eu policies. it calls for the urban specificity to be taken into better account in all european policies. it advocates the inclusion of the urban dimension in all european policies by taking into account ‘the urban acquis’ and in each case carrying out impact studies on small, medium and large-sized cities.
