the rapporteur. - mr president, i must say at the outset that the interest in my report has exceeded expectations. whether it's the fruitful collaboration with colleagues, for which i thank them so much, or the exchanges of ideas, or the hard-fought battles for every word with other colleagues. i'm so glad my report didn't fall through. it is clear that the issue of employment and the future of work in europe is of concern to all of us. europe is facing many serious challenges today. we all know where our future efforts will have to go. the key issue to which we must also give due attention is the creation of new jobs, the reduction of unemployment and the building of a competitive labour market reflecting the real needs of the present. young europeans in particular are currently suffering from unemployment, which is the result of a certain stagnation or reluctance on the part of some countries to embark on long-term labour market reforms or modernisation of labour law, many of whose provisions date back to our grandparents. we must work together to respond much more flexibly to the needs of the 21st century. the alarming youth unemployment figures in southern europe are a signal that the youngest generation is losing the traditional transition from school to work, losing their career dreams and with them their trust in the system. we 're running out of time . let's stop this from happening, and together, we can change it. but progress is impossible without change. what we need is a competitive job market. a labour market that will be modernised and that will constantly change and develop in line with the times in which we live, and not stagnate in history. a labour market which will seek to match the skills of jobseekers with the supply of vacancies, i.e. a market which will monitor and evaluate the real needs of employers and adapt the vocational training supply accordingly. therefore, lifelong learning is of utmost importance, enabling people of all ages to keep pace with the challenges of their careers. let us not be afraid to look for examples of good practice and let them inspire us. as for the vote on my report, we can argue on every point. some people do not like the idea that young people should be responsible for their lives and should prepare actively and responsibly for inclusion in the work process. some have reservations about the economic mobility of workers within eu countries. others may disagree with the proposed changes and procedures to stabilise and develop the situation in europe's labour markets. but this is no time to argue over words and numbers. now we have to decide: are we capable of accepting reality? look at the situation without political bias? do we really want to build a competitive labour market together? if we continue on the same path and do the same things in the same way, change will never come. this is no longer about whether we want to go more left or more right. we all have to go forward now. whatever the outcome of tomorrow's vote, i will not relent in my initiative. i will also look at how to link the education system to the needs of the labour market and how to motivate young europeans to live an active life. after all, we spend a third of our lives in the workplace and this experience is irreplaceable for any human being. we cannot think that all we need is to protect our citizens and their labour rights. we would be acting like an overly caring mother who lovingly cares for her children but fails to teach them the right skills for life. we must have the ambition to raise self-confident citizens, modern europeans, who are well prepared for life and who are not afraid to take responsibility for themselves and for others. we must want to educate europeans who have a clear vision of their future and are able to fight for it. my report is, i believe, the first step in the right direction on this road.
mr president, i would like to support the reports by our colleagues martina dlabajová and verónica lope fontagné. i am convinced they are important and i am glad that our group, the epp group, is ready to support them. i am in complete agreement with the main points of the reports. skills mismatch is a major problem in terms of a competitive workforce and a flexible labour market in europe. if europe wants to fight unemployment, especially youth unemployment, and if it wants to continue to play a crucial role in the world economy, it needs to adopt policies which will focus on good skills and competencies. i agree that we should work on increasing the mobility of workers and on cooperation between schools and the productive sector, providing practical experience to students. i am delighted that yesterday parliament approved my report on promoting youth entrepreneurship through education and training. parliament called for entrepreneurship skills to be included in school curricula, and this is precisely the right step for increasing the competitiveness of young graduates in the labour market. entrepreneurship skills, such as a sense of initiative, risk taking, resilience, and financial and ict literacy, are quite universal and can be used both in entrepreneurship activity and by employers. i am happy to see that the report by my colleague ms dlabajová mentions the importance of fostering entrepreneurial spirit among european youth, and i also see great potential in providing more opportunities for women, who form the majority of university graduates.

in writing. the eu's transport policy faces major challenges in the form of a shift towards more sustainable and energy-efficient modes of transport, the construction of modern infrastructure and the completion of the trans-european transport network. in this context, the report on the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport rightly points to the need to develop the market for electric vehicles and alternative fuels (electricity, hydrogen, natural gas cng and lng, sustainable biofuels, in particular biofuels produced from waste and processing residues, including molasses-based ethanol) and to accelerate the deployment of the necessary infrastructure for vehicle charging and refuelling. more efforts are needed to promote the development of sustainable electromobility across the union. on the other hand, i am convinced that the report does not call on the commission to adopt, if necessary, support measures to prevent the emergence of differences between the social conditions of road transport in the various member states in order to prevent so-called social dumping. social dumping is a concept that is being abused to discriminate against czech road hauliers, and i am very strongly against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport, which assesses the current strategy of european transport policy. the strategy aims to create an area that ensures the free movement of services and the opening of transport markets, the so-called single european transport market. the strategy also aims to achieve a competitive and resource-efficient transport system and the related efforts to reduce emissions. the report also focuses on measures to improve road safety, in particular by reducing the number of deaths on european roads. this report emphasises the need to complete safe and quality infrastructure in all modes of transport within the ten-t network, including the removal of cross-border barriers. structural changes in transport can improve quality of life and the environment, while preserving people's freedom of movement and the competitiveness of eu industry.

member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank in particular the rapporteur, ms rozière, for her report on the establishment of a geographical indication protection system at eu level for non-agricultural products. the commission had decided to put this idea to the test through a green paper and a public consultation in summer 2014. the results of the consultation, published in june of this year, were supportive of such a system. let me remind you what the situation is about. a geographical indication identifies goods as originating from a country, region or locality where a particular quality, reputation or other characteristic of the product is linked to its geographical origin: for example, bordeaux wine, murano glass or irish whiskey. agriculture products such as cheeses, wines, meats, fruits and vegetables from a specific geographical origin, possessing certain qualities or made according to traditional methods, may be afforded eu-wide geographical indication protection. however, non-agricultural products, such as ceramics, marble, cutlery, shoes, tapestries and musical instruments, do not, to date, enjoy unitary geographical indication protection at eu level beyond national laws. that is, for instance, the case of carrara marble from italy, solingen knives from germany, koniaków lace from poland or haapsalu mud from estonia. moving towards a system of non-agricultural geographical indications would be a major step, the costs and benefits of which would need to be assessed very carefully. what we do know is that direct and indirect employment in the sectors producing geographically-rooted non-agricultural products has been estimated at around four million jobs. on the positive side, i can see four benefits. first, safeguarding jobs and wealth in economically fragile areas: two-thirds of the regions from which non-agricultural geographical indication products originate have a poverty rate or an unemployment rate above 20%. second, encouraging tourism: geographical indication products have always been innovating using traditional knowhow or cultural heritage. the underlying image of quality can have a significant impact on the attractiveness of regions at local and international level. third, increasing the distinctiveness and attraction of the relevant products would help increase sales volumes and thus the competitiveness of european businesses – mostly small and medium enterprises – as was the case for agricultural products. fourth, helping consumers make more informed choices while preventing fraudulent use of geographical indications. beyond these issues and as your report also points out, there would be positive effects on trade relations with third countries too. indeed, an eu-wide protection system could positively impact our bilateral negotiations with emerging and developing countries interested in securing better protection for their geographical indication products in the eu. at multilateral level in the world trade organisation, the eu’s negotiating efforts to improve the level of protection for geographical indications would also benefit from an extension of the protection to non-agricultural products. however, there are also drawbacks. such a system would imply quite far-reaching regulatory intervention, the proportionality of which will need to be assessed very carefully. your report brings an important input to the ongoing reflection on an eu-wide protection system for non-agricultural geographical indications. the commission will consider your recommendations with attention and will continue to reflect, with all interested parties, on a possible way forward.
in writing.– expanding the eu system of geographical indicators to include non-agricultural goods would mean greater protection, transparency and information for both eu consumers and producers. european consumers will be better informed about the quality and origin of the product they are buying. the skills of producers will be recognised and protected in a more coherent manner. by also securing the prestige of local european handicraft, this could, importantly, help in bringing growth and securing jobs in the local areas that produce these products. in order to feel the full economic benefits of this eu-wide protection, we must ensure that information on the system reaches all consumers and producers. a unitary eu level of protection, however, should not mean the elimination of protection at national level. not all producers will need protection at eu level, particularly those who run their business in only one state. the eu unitary system should thus coexist with the member state level so that producers may choose the type of protection that will best meet their needs.

in writing. ‒ i fully supported the council decision authorising the member states to ratify the 2014 ilo forced labour convention in order to promote the combat of this criminal phenomenon which is unfortunately still present in contemporary europe. the steps to be undertaken will protect the victims of forced labour and fight human trafficking as well as the black market in general.
in writing. on 6 october 2015, at the strasbourg plenary, i supported the recommendation on a draft council decision authorising member states to ratify, in the interest of the eu, the 2014 protocol to the international labour organisation convention on forced labour, 1930, as regards articles 1 to 4. the forced labour convention is one of the eight core conventions of the international labour organisation and is considered an instrument for the protection and promotion of human rights. the protocol seeks to address shortcomings in the implementation of the convention and to make progress in the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of forced labour (slavery) as well as in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. the ratification of this protocol is an important step in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in ensuring the rights of victims of crime across europe. it is therefore of the utmost importance that all member states proceed to the accelerated ratification of the protocol, as this will greatly facilitate the fight against trafficking in human beings. which, in the light of today's migration crisis, where organised crime on a mass scale is essentially trafficking in human beings, is exactly one of the measures that the eu today urgently needs. as all our members supported this recommendation in the previous vote in the libe committee, i could not have voted otherwise in the plenary vote.
in writing. the forced labour convention is one of the eight core ilo conventions that constitute the basic international labour standards and is considered a human rights instrument. by adopting this convention in 1930, the international labour organization called on states to prohibit the use of forced labor as soon as possible and to criminalize it as a crime. eighty years later, the ilo estimates that at least 20.9 million people worldwide are victims of forced labor. the protocol seeks to address implementation gaps and to make progress in the prevention of trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation, as well as in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. i am convinced that ratification of the protocol by eu member states will facilitate the fight against trafficking in human beings, which is why i supported this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i am proud of parliaments’ vote on the ilo forced labour convention recommendation. the european union is a force for human rights and this vote further supports that. the ilo estimates that there are still at least 20.9 million people who are victims of forced labour, and this comes 80 years after the initial adoption of the convention. this protocol will help fill in the gaps in the implementation to help prevent the trafficking of labour exploitation. i support the calls for ilo member states to develop a national policy for the constant subduing of forced labour. in addition, the measure also helps the victims of forced labour be released, protected and rehabilitated, as well as allowing them other assistance. this protocol is based on fundamental human rights, and i believe that it will help to fight the trafficking of victims. this convention is just as important today as it was almost a century ago.

in writing. ‒ i supported this report aiming to subject 4-methylamphetamine to control measures. the substance 4-methylamphetamine emerged on the illicit amphetamine market in 2009. by the time of an eu risk-assessment in 2012, it had been detected in 15 member states and there had been a total of 21 fatalities registered in four member states related to its abuse. the controls are especially desirable because of the health risks it poses, especially when used in combination with other substances, its strong resemblance in appearance and effects with amphetamine, the fact that users may consume it unknowingly, and its limited medical value or use.
in writing. ‒ the substance 5-(2-aminopropyl)indole appears to be a stimulant substance that may also have hallucinogenic effects. it is commercially available on the internet and from ‘head shops’, marketed as a ‘research chemical’. a total of 24 fatalities have been registered in four member states from april to august 2012 in relation to it. the available scientific evidence provides sufficient grounds for subjecting 5-(2-aminopropyl)indole to control measures across the european union. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed this report seeking to put potentially dangerous new psychoactive substances under control. the substance 25i-nbome is a classical serotonergic hallucinogen, which has been subject to control measures and criminal sanctions at eu level from 2003. ah-7921 is a structurally atypical synthetic opioid analgesic commonly known as 'doxylam'. it can be easily confused with ‘doxylamine’, an anti-histaminic medicine with sedative-hypnotic properties, which could lead to unintentional overdoses. mdpv is a ring-substituted synthetic derivative of cathinone chemically related to pyrovalerone, which are both subject to control under the 1971 united nations convention on psychotropic substances. one hundred and eight fatalities were registered in eight member states and norway between september 2009 and august 2013 relating to it. methoxetamine is a substance which is chemically similar to ketamine and the internationally-controlled substance phencyclidine (pcp). twenty deaths associated with methoxetamine have been reported by six member states. the risk assessment recommended by the council concluded that these substances should be put under control to minimise the health and social risk they cause.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which supports subjecting 4,4'-dmar and mt-45 to control measures across the eu. the substances 4,4'-dmar and mt-45 are new psychoactive substances. while more research is needed, available evidence suggests they pose health and social risk. the substance 4,4'-dmar emerged on the new psychoactive substances market in 2012 as a ‘research chemical’ sold by internet retailers, and it is now available on the street market. there have been 31 deaths associated with 4,4'-dmar registered in three member states, between june 2013 and june 2014. mt-45 was invented in the early 1970s. a total of 28 fatalities due to mt-45 occurring between november 2013 and july 2014 have been reported by one member state.

in writing. ‒ geographical indications (gis) is a sign used to help consumer identify food products whose qualities or reputation are recognised as unique to their particular country, region or town of origin. this indication allows the czech republic to protect its well-known beers, wines and liqueurs, for example. the registered products then receive an eu high level of recognition and protection. regional artisanal products however, are not covered by the european gi system. the manufacturers thus have to register them in each member states, and adapt to very different national registration procedures. i see the extension of the system to non-agricultural products as logical next step as it will protect manufacturers from unfair competition, boost local production while providing consumers with better information about the origin of the artisanal products they buy. for these reasons, i decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. a geographical indication refers to goods originating in a country, region or place where the quality, reputation or other characteristic of the product is associated with its geographical origin. examples include bordeaux wine, murano glass or parma ham. agricultural products of specific geographical origin, such as cheese, wine, meat, fruit and vegetables, which have certain characteristics or are produced by traditional methods, can be granted pan-european protection of a geographical indication, such as parmesan cheese. non-agricultural products such as ceramics, marble, carpentry, footwear, tapestries or musical instruments are not yet granted uniform protection by geographical indications at eu level beyond national legislation. because i believe that the eu can boast of a wealth of non-agricultural products, whether it be czech crystal or kara marble, and that our unique and diverse heritage must be protected, i voted in favour.

for the group gue/ngl. mr president, as i said, we are discussing today an amendment to the so-called european small claims procedure. the procedure is designed as an alternative to ordinary litigation under the code of civil procedure. it aims in particular to help consumers to exercise their rights in cross-border disputes and to improve access to legal protection for smes in the recovery of small claims. the amendment to the regulation aims to remove some of the problems which the procedure has faced since its inception in 2009, namely: first, the setting of a limit on court fees, the amount of which has often discouraged consumers from using the procedure; second, the limit of eur 2 000 for small and medium-sized enterprises to amend, as only a small percentage of their cross-border claims have reached that limit. the outcome of the trialogue represents, in my view, a balanced compromise that responds to the practical needs of the parties and facilitates effective access to justice for consumers and smes. i thank the rapporteur and all the shadow rapporteurs, the secretariat of our committee for the work they have done and i support the motion.

in writing. on 7 october 2015, we voted in strasbourg on the report on the draft regulation amending the regulation establishing the so-called european small claims procedure and the european order for payment procedure. it should be noted that the european small claims procedure is an increasingly used alternative to ordinary civil litigation. it was introduced in particular to help consumers to exercise their rights in crossborder disputes. after five years of application of the original regulation, the european small claims procedure has proved to be a useful and necessary tool. however, during that period, certain problems with this adjustment became apparent. the amendment aims to remove some of the problems that the procedure has faced since its inception, namely to set a limit on court fees, the excessive amount of which has discouraged consumers from using this type of procedure, and to adjust the limit of eur 2 000 for smes, which has been very restrictive to them because only a small percentage of their cross-border claims have been covered. i voted in favour of the report because the outcome of the trilogue is a fairly balanced compromise which will hopefully facilitate access to justice for consumers and smes alike. moreover, the final text is of far better quality than the text originally issued by the committee.
in writing. ‒ the small claims procedure is an alternative to the civil procedure which has been in place since 2009. today we discussed its amendment, which is intended to respond in particular to the needs of consumers and smes, who were discouraged by too high court fees and, conversely, by too low a limit by which small and medium-sized claims are defined. those amendments should allow in particular smes to recover more of their claims through proceedings. i consider the text presented to be a balanced compromise, the result of a well-done work in the trilogue, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. i supported the agreement reached by the ep and the council at first reading, which significantly improves the current legislation in force since 2009. in my view, this amendment will lead to greater use of the small claims procedure, as consumers will no longer be deterred by excessive court fees, which often exceed the amount recovered, and small and medium-sized enterprises will not be constrained by the current limit of eur 2 000, which many of their crossborder claims do not fit, thanks to the agreed increase to eur 5 000. i see the small claims procedure as an example of useful eu legislation that has been shown to make life easier for citizens and businesses when they are involved in a dispute with a cross-border dimension.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that the european parliament has today approved legislation to further reduce emissions. there are currently two directives setting limits for small and large combustion plants, which have now been supplemented by emission limits for medium-sized plants (combined plants with a total rated thermal input of 1 mw or more but less than 50 mw). improving air quality is one of the long-term priorities of the social democrats, and further emission reductions are a key prerequisite. i too have long supported legislation in favour of strict emission limits, but it can only be effective if it affects all producers and not just some of them. the gap between small and large producers therefore needed to be filled and i'm glad that it finally happened today. i also see today's decision as a strong signal of the eu's clear priorities on air protection ahead of the upcoming climate summit in paris.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report with the view to fill a legislation gap in which emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants are generally not yet regulated at the eu level. the directive proposal is designed to reduce pollution by nox, so2 and dust by setting limit values for new and existing installations, together with a simple registration scheme, in order to help deliver a significant part of member states’ emission reduction obligations and avoid possible trade-offs between air quality and increased biomass use, which may result in higher air pollution. the directive should apply to combinations formed by two or more combustion plants having a total rated thermal input equal to or greater than 1 mw and less than 50 mw, unless the combination is a combustion plant covered by chapter iii of directive 2010/75/eu on industrial emissions.
in writing. - i supported this report. as shown by individual measurements in the border areas of the member states, some areas suffer from significant air pollution. pollution from one country thus ends up in another country, often with different national exemptions. trying to solve this resource-scarcity problem is certainly important. of course, it's complicated to rationally influence small resources. but at the same time, limiting emissions from a large number of these sources over a large area is a real problem. to achieve real results in reducing air pollution, the issue needs to be approached in a comprehensive way, so that it is not just an administrative regulation, but that the incentives, including the necessary education, accompany each step. there is also a need to stimulate interest in modernising these sources, whether by promoting innovation or, for example, research into modern energy sources meeting the required stricter limits.
in writing. ‒ as i said a few weeks ago in the debate on food origin labelling, i fully support the idea of introducing common pan-european requirements for transparent food labelling. these measures are one of the key factors in protecting the health of our population. the proposal aims in particular to ensure that consumers are properly informed about the food they consume. although it is not expected that caseins and caseinates will be sold to the final consumer but only between food business operators, it is still important that food business operators have at their disposal the information they need to label the final products, in particular as regards allergens. if the mandatory information referred to in the directive is not provided on the packaging, these products cannot be placed on the market at all. proper labelling of caseins and caseinates will enable consumers, and in particular those suffering from food allergies or intolerances, to make informed choices. given that we have had a number of serious scandals in the czech republic in recent years over the quality, composition and origin of the food sold there, and i believe that we are not alone in the pan-european context, i intend to fully support this proposal and any other efforts which, by helping to improve consumer information, will ultimately also lead to an improvement in the quality of what we eat.
in writing. ‒ i agree that it is important for the health and well-being of consumers that they know what they are consuming. however, i do not agree with this proposal because the member states are perfectly capable of dealing with this matter themselves. there is no reason for the european union to be concerned. i'm against the new european legislation.
in writing. ‒ caseins and caseinates are lactoproteins that are sold from businesses to businesses for the preparation of food products. the proposal for a directive seeks alignment of the compositional requirements for edible caseins to the codex alimentarius, which would help ensure a level playing field for food businesses on the world market. it also sets out labelling requirements for caseins and caseinates which will enable consumers, and particularly those suffering from a food allergy or intolerance, to make informed choices. i therefore supported this report.
in writing. on 7 october 2015, at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg, we voted on the report on the draft regulation amending the regulation laying down the financial rules for the general budget of the eu. this is a very technical innovation which had to be implemented in particular to make access to eu funds easier, more reliable, more efficient and at the same time to prevent misuse of these funds. in addition, it was also necessary to adapt this regulation to the new eu directives on public procurement and on the award of concessions by the authorities. i rather see the changes made positively, as they generally simplify the procedures and rules concerning the eligibility and non-eligibility criteria for eu concession contracts. in particular, i see positively that the criteria for excluding a participant from eu bodies' procurement procedures include past tax fraud, tax evasion, including tax evasion through tax-exempt offshore structures or misappropriation of public funds. the report goes into such detail that it addresses and distinguishes between different types of 'conflict of interest' and serious professional misconduct by officials or representatives of eu institutions. given these positive changes, i voted in favour of the motion.

member of the commission.– mr president, on behalf of my colleague commissioner elżbieta bieńkowska, i am here to discuss this issue. the issue raised by the honourable members touches at the heart of what eu citizens can expect of the single market. when shopping cross-border, our consumers are still being discriminated against on the basis of their nationality or place of residence. this is not acceptable. we keep on receiving complaints from citizens against alleged discriminatory practices, through various channels. first, direct complaints; second, complaints to european consumer centres; third, information requests to your europe advice; and, fourth and most importantly, parliamentary questions. as democratically elected representatives, you act as a major interface between citizens and eu institutions. i cannot encourage you strongly enough to keep on sending us feedback from your constituents. with the rise of the internet, e-commerce is getting increasingly important, but many questions also concern transactions taking place on commercial premises. online geo-blocking is one of the most visible and the most often described types of discrimination, with consumers being barred from completing transactions, or being redirected to another website offering the same service but at a higher price. discrimination also takes place on a daily basis for millions of europeans travelling abroad as tourists, buying a second home in another country, or just crossing the border. this must stop – and action has been announced in the digital single market strategy. the need for action will be expanded on in the internal market strategy for goods and services, to be adopted at the end of the month. on 24 september 2015, the commission also launched a public consultation. the consultation will help the commission prepare a legislative initiative in 2016. we all know examples of discriminatory practices. last year, we initiated an action with the main car rental companies in europe, after noticing very substantial price differences for exactly the same service, just depending on the place of residence of the customer. this year, you will have heard of press reports concerning a major amusement park in france, for which some special offers were limited to french residents. we also have examples of people being denied access to car-sharing with a non-national driving licence, or for the need to have a national registration number to buy a service. the current legal framework has not created enough certainty for businesses and consumers. it has not enabled national authorities to enforce the non-discrimination obligation in daily practice. this is what we are planning to address. contractual freedom is an important principle, which must be preserved, but we must also tackle the voluntary segmentation of the single market by companies, and we must safeguard the rights of consumers. the interests of smes must also be protected. we want to encourage companies and consumers to use the single market, not force them to do so if it would be too burdensome or uncertain for them. my colleagues elżbieta bieńkowska and günther öttinger will be more than happy to discuss those challenges further in order to find solutions that open up the single market for companies and consumers alike.

in writing. ‒ equal treatment of men and women is one of the fundamental principles of the eu law. we might not believe it but in 2015 the average gender pay gap in the eu is still above 16%, going as high as one-third of pay in some member states. as a result of the adoption of various instruments at national and eu level and of the consistent application by the courts of the principles of anti-discrimination laid down in article 157 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and in directive 2006/54/ec, we have come a long way forward on eliminating gender pay gap in salaries and pensions. however, what we need to fight more than ever are the stereotypes. if society is not ready to mature by overcoming traditional thinking, we will not be able to eliminate practices which belong to history. despite many positive elements outlined in this report, i took a decision to abstain on the final vote. simply i do not believe that financial sanctions and administrative burden on companies or binding quotas can fight the stereotypes which are at the core of direct and indirect discrimination on pay.
in writing. i voted against this report, which is so incredible and bizarre that it could only have been born in the completely detached environment of the brussels eurocracy. for the purpose of this explanation, i will select a few of the most egregious points: point 16 calls on the commission and the member states to take measures to monitor and control, by setting up effective monitoring systems, in order to improve the collection of data on harassment and discrimination cases, calls on the commission to closely monitor the effectiveness of national complaint handling bodies and their procedures in relation to the application of the directives on gender equality in matters of gender identity, expression and gender reassignment, and to support and encourage member states in the inclusion of transgender and intersex persons in diversity training; point 36 calls on the member states to [...] make it compulsory for companies to draw up and implement annual gender equality business plans, 41 calls on the member states to take the necessary measures to reverse the burden of proof so as to ensure that it is always the employer who will have to prove that the difference in treatment found does not lead to any discrimination (the rule of law is clearly something unacceptable in brussels) and paragraph 45 stresses that one of the best ways to achieve this objective has proved to be through binding quotas.
in writing. i supported the report on equal opportunities in employment and occupation because i believe that this issue needs to be given increased attention. i did so even though not every part of the final report corresponded to my views, but i still felt it necessary to support the report. the principle of equal pay should be the main priority, but it is also important to combat other obstacles to equal treatment, such as discrimination in pension schemes. i believe that, overall, there is a need to increase women's involvement in the management and governance of companies and enterprises, both to ensure their equal status and to fully exploit their abilities and potential.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that parliament has voted favourably on the report on equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation. gender equality is something which the eu strives to achieve – as do i – and this measure helps to address some of the gaps that are still prevalent in the workplace. the report stresses the importance of fighting indirect discrimination, especially with regard to pension schemes. it also calls on the commission and member states to raise awareness regarding the pay and pensions gaps between the genders. in addition, it recommends that member states become role models within their own public institutions when it comes to equal pay for women. i am proud of the result of the vote on this report, and i believe that it will bring meaningful change and help with closing the gender gap.
in writing. all women can be victims of pay discrimination in the workplace. the fact that they receive less pay for comparable work than men has a significant impact on their social security in old age, among other things. it is unacceptable that women receive an average of 39% less pension than men. i therefore consider it necessary to introduce the principle of equal opportunities and equal treatment in employment for men and women and therefore welcome the proposal for this report. employers should not only pay equal pay regardless of gender, but also increase the representation of women in senior positions.
in writing. ‒ in today's vote on the amendments to the report on equal opportunities and equal treatment for men and women in employment and occupation, i voted to reaffirm my position, as i have expressed it in previous votes on similar cases, that in certain bioethical issues or family policy issues the subsidiarity principle should be applied consistently and that these issues should not be confused with issues which are the subject of other reports or opinions of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report is concerned with the gender pay gap and discrimination in the workplace. it states that – in spite of eu efforts throughout the last 40 years, eu primary legislation and case law – the gender pay gap still exists, at an average of 16.4 % across the eu. the report therefore calls on the commission to prepare a new legislative proposal that would necessitate observance of the principle of equal pay. while i wholly subscribe to the concept of equal treatment of men and women in employment and otherwise, i have difficulties with some of the specific measures proposed by this report. in particular, i do not fully identify with the recommendation of binding quotas, which the report considers as the best way to increase women’s involvement in political and economic decision making. i therefore abstained from voting on this report.

in writing. since the adoption of the accompanying directive in 2004, the tourism sector has changed considerably. in particular, consumers are increasingly choosing to buy their travel arrangements via the internet, where the retailer is able to tailor the trip to each individual customer, but this also carries a number of risks in the form of unclear, misleading or incomplete information provided by the retailer of the products offered. the aim of the amendment of the directive must be to increase transparency and thus ultimately to increase the protection of the client, that is to say the consumer. the directive thus introduces, for example, an obligation to inform travellers before making a payment whether they have chosen a package or linked travel service and, if so, what their level of protection is. i agree with the vast majority of the elements contained in the amended text, for example that key information such as essential travel services or prices contained in advertising material, on the organiser's website or in catalogues as part of the pre-contractual information should be binding unless the organiser reserves the right to change these elements and clearly communicates this to the traveller before the contract is concluded. furthermore, the passenger's right to withdraw from the contract should be clearly formulated. i backed the text.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that travellers who organise their own holidays and buy accommodation or a plane ticket through linked websites will have the same rights to protection in the european union as travel agency clients. the new rules take account of the increase in the number of people who book their holidays on-line with linked service providers. the commission will also consider the possibility of a new contract for the provision of services to passengers, in particular for the provision of services to the public, to be a package contract. organisers and retailers will have to make clear to passengers that they are package services and inform them of who is responsible in the event of complications.
in writing. i supported the final text of the package travel directive because it is necessary to adapt the rules to the current trends of greater use of the internet as a tool for holiday making, from travel, to accommodation, to ancillary services such as car rental at the place of stay. consumers who book travel services through packages and via the internet will enjoy the same levels of protection as those who use the services of traditional travel agents. i consider that the important provisions that have been successfully put to the european parliament are, in particular, the provision of clear and unambiguous information on the travel package and liability in the event of complications, the possibility of withdrawing from the contract in the event of a substantial change in commercial conditions, and a higher level of protection for passengers in the event of their inability to return due to unavoidable and unforeseeable circumstances.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed this report, because i appreciate its contribution to the better protection of citizens who buy their holidays online. the aim of the report is to adopt a directive on package travel and linked travel arrangements, amending regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 and directive 2011/83/eu of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directive 90/314/eec. the revised laws improve consumer rights, by putting in place stricter controls on price surcharges, a requirement to pass on price reductions to customers, compensation for non-material damages and refunds of all payments in case providers go bankrupt.

in writing. i welcome the compromise reached in the report on the single market for electronic communications. after delays caused by the council, the european public will finally get to see the long-promised abolition of roaming charges. it is commendable that the rapporteur and his shadow colleagues have made this a common priority. as regards net neutrality, i supported some of the amendments tabled by the greens and gue/ngl groups, as i believe they provide a clearer definition of net neutrality and at the same time allow member states to strengthen the proposed measures. it is important that europe sets fair standards for network transmission.
in writing. ‒ i have been in favour of abolishing roaming charges from the outset. however, the result achieved in the council has, in my view, in principle nothing in common with the original ambitious objectives set by the european parliament in 2011. the resulting text still leaves room for fees, just with a different name. at the same time, it is absolutely essential for me to fight for the principle of so-called net neutrality, which simply means the principle of equality of data transmitted over the internet, that is, internet providers must treat traffic on their networks in the same way, that is, they cannot offer users an internet service faster than some companies and get paid by these companies. net neutrality means that all data transmitted over this line is sent with the same priority. thus, there cannot be a situation where, for example, one data package is given priority over another on the basis of content, origin or type of service. the opposite of net neutrality would be a situation where a company could subscribe to a privilege for its services at the expense of the services of other companies. this would slow down competition, which could not afford to pay the fee. in the course of the discussions with the council, it became clear that the latter was not prepared to accept a clear definition of the term in the proposal. for this reason, i could not support the text in its current form.
in writing. i supported the report which brings the abolition of roaming charges to 14 june 2017. since the phasing out of roaming charges, i promise an increase in mobile phone usage when travelling abroad. statistics show that half of people do not use mobile data services when abroad, and instead access the internet through other means than their mobile phone. this forced change in consumer behaviour will no longer be necessary, as consumers will no longer be discouraged by higher telephone charges when abroad. the end of roaming charges could have come sooner, but in the context of complicated negotiations with the member states, this is a compromise which i regard as a successful outcome. the obligation on the provider to inform the consumer of the minimum and maximum data rates that he can expect before signing the contract also strengthens the consumer's rights. if the connection provider then fails to comply, this will be grounds for withdrawal from the contract.
in writing. i supported the final form of the so-called telecommunications package because it would bring two major benefits to consumers. this is the latest step in a long-running effort by the social democrats group in the european parliament to end roaming charges and break down the illogical artificial borders for mobile communications within the eu. the provisions on ensuring net neutrality through an open internet based on non-discrimination, transparency and clear end-user rights are equally important. for the first time, this will be a rule in european legislation that internet access service providers must treat all traffic equally.
in writing. i supported today's legislative resolution of the european parliament on the single european market for electronic communications, in particular because it represents a long-awaited and necessary step towards the abolition of roaming charges. i regret that the compromise adopted did not contain an explicit definition of net neutrality, but this principle was reflected in the specific provisions of the compromise and i consider the abolition of roaming charges across the european union to be an important example of the added value that the european union can bring. the abolition of roaming charges covers both calling, sms and data services and will take effect from 15 june 2017. today's vote thus represents an important moment in the process of building a european digital single market. however, it is important for the future that the european commission strictly monitors the proper implementation of these rules so that the desired effect is actually achieved.

in writing. ‒ today we discussed a report which aims to contribute to the protection of human rights through the control of goods or activities that are or could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the eu has a long-standing policy to end the use of the death penalty worldwide and to prevent torture. they seek to achieve these objectives through prohibitions linked to licensing requirements for trade in listed goods. it governs the prohibition of trade in 'single-use' goods intended for torture and the execution of the death penalty and related technical assistance (annex ii) and the system for approving 'dual-use' goods that could be misused for torture and the execution of the death penalty by lethal injection (annex iii). i believe that the revision of the eu-wide controls on trade in torture instruments should have been done a long time ago and is a step in the right direction, which is why i supported the report in the final vote.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims at strengthening the controls of torture tools. the report seeks to amend council regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 concerning trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, known as the ‘anti-torture regulation’. the ‘anti-torture regulation’ contributes to the eu policy of eliminating death penalty worldwide, and of preventing torture. it helps achieve these goals by combining prohibitions with licensing requirements for trade in listed goods. it governs a ban of trade in ‘single-use’ torture and execution items and related technical assistance and an authorisation system for ‘multi-purpose’ items that could be misused for torture and executions by lethal injections.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because an increase in transparency concerning tax rulings is needed. the report seeks to amend directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, as regards mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. the reason is that currently, member states share very little information with one another about their tax rulings. as a result, they do not spontaneously exchange their tax rulings and are often unaware of cross-border tax rulings issued elsewhere in the eu which may impact their own tax bases. to bring more transparency, the mechanisms established by council directive 2011/16/eu need to be enhanced. regarding some of the european parliament’s amendments to the commission proposal, it agreed that the directive should apply to all tax rulings and not just cross border rulings and advance pricing arrangements, since purely national transactions can also have cross-border effects.

in writing. ‒ eniac is part of the so-called eu joint undertakings, in which other partners (in this case the eu member states) are involved, has financial autonomy but is subject to the eu's budgetary discharge. the discharge for the eniac joint undertaking for 2013 was postponed in april this year. the reason for the delay was mainly the european court of auditors' repeated concern about the ex post audit strategy, which relies heavily on the project cost statements of the national funding bodies and thus does not provide sufficient assurance as to the legality and regularity of the operations carried out. eniac has taken significant measures to improve the situation in the meantime, which include the introduction of a specific reporting form to increase this certainty, and are complemented by the evaluation of the national guarantee schemes by the joint undertaking and by visits by the court of auditors to the national funding bodies. the committee on budgetary control, of which i am a member, considered the additional information to be sufficient to grant discharge. that is why i voted in committee and in plenary to grant discharge. i am continuously monitoring the situation with regard to the eu joint undertakings intensively from my position as shadow rapporteur for the 2014 discharge of the eu joint undertakings.

in writing. - today we discussed a report that i attach particular importance to because of my medical profession. the ebola outbreak in africa last year showed that health systems in the most affected countries show huge gaps. the most affected countries, with around 80% of their citizens living in extreme poverty, were already among the countries with the lowest human development index according to the undp survey data before the outbreak and had the highest mortality rates in the world for premature babies, adults and children under five, mainly due to treatable diseases. i am convinced of the need to address social inequalities in order to build a strong and sustainable public health system, and in this regard i welcome the idea of introducing publicly funded universal health care, provided free of charge at the point of delivery, and i join the urgent call on the commission to present, together with partner countries and other donors, as soon as possible a programme for the introduction of universal health insurance, which would guarantee the distribution of health risks. this crisis has also been systemic in terms of its global management. it took the international community a long time to grasp the gravity of the situation and to respond. we have no choice but to learn from the past crisis and take measures to prevent its recurrence. i voted for the report.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the european parliament today approved legislation to further support countries affected by the humanitarian crisis caused by the worst ebola outbreak in history. the main countries concerned are sierra leone, liberia and guinea. other assistance should focus on strengthening health and education systems in affected countries, in addition to the fight against the disease itself. the european union has invested €1.2 billion in the fight against ebola since the crisis began. but as it turned out, the concrete steps came too late. the epidemic has taken and is taking a huge toll not only on patients, but also on their families. this is why we need to learn as much as possible from the developments and take concrete action in the future on how the eu should behave in similar situations. the focus now must be on providing adequate support for research and prevention of ebola and other similarly dangerous diseases.
in writing. i supported today's report by the european parliament on the ebola crisis. i believe that its subtitle 'learning for the future and how to improve healthcare systems in developing countries to prevent future crises' sums up well the european parliament's intention to take stock of this experience and to focus development aid efforts on helping to stabilise the fragile health systems of not only the epidemic-stricken african countries. this effort to increase assistance to the health sector must be accompanied by the fight against poverty and the promotion of an efficient and non-corrupt public administration. this is about saving lives, but it is also about minimising the complications that any similar epidemic would also cause in the member states in the areas of tourism, transport in general, mobilisation of public health and safety institutions, etc. it is therefore not just about the conditions at the source of the outbreak and the removal of the causes, but also about the preparedness of the competent authorities of the member states and their sufficient coordination within the eu in the event of an outbreak.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on a joint motion for a resolution on emission measurement in the automotive sector. i think there are a number of ways of looking at this phenomenon. in any event, any fraud with emission limits must be condemned and thoroughly investigated. furthermore, the protection of consumers must be borne in mind, who must retain the right to choose the product of their choice depending on the complex technical characteristics communicated to them. we also have to realize that the automotive industry is dominated by large multinational companies, so it's not just an eu problem. it should also be taken into account that the automotive industry in some member states makes a major contribution to promoting employment and innovation growth. the automotive supply industry is dominated by small and medium-sized enterprises. the economic strength of many regions in europe is based on the automotive industry and automotive supply industries. the current scandal threatens to seriously damage the reputation of the entire industry. we must try to remedy this situation, but preferably with a balanced approach that does not damage the automotive sector any further. i think that the text presented today is not balanced in this respect and that some of the objectives it contains are not achievable, so i abstained in the final vote on the resolution.
in writing. i supported the resolution on emission measurements in the motor vehicle industry because i am one of those who are calling for the current dieselgate emissions scandal to be taken to its logical conclusion and for clear ways of improving the situation to be found. it is therefore appropriate to call on the commission to adopt and implement without delay a new test cycle based on real-world emission measurements. in this respect, however, i was not pleasantly surprised by the recently announced agreement between the member states and the commission on the setting of relatively soft conditions for newly introduced car emission tests (this is the link between road tests and laboratory tests). i'm not sure this is the right way to restore consumer confidence in diesel engines and the automotive industry in general and to ensure the air quality that can be achieved with today's state of the art technology.
in writing. i supported today's european parliament resolution on dieselgate, which clearly condemns the false information and customer fraud perpetrated by volkswagen. the manipulation of information on their cars' emissions has a major impact on the environment and on the health of citizens, and it is important to remember that limits are not there to burden manufacturers, but to protect the environment for all of us. of course, the whole affair will not go without significant economic repercussions not only for the carmaker in question, but possibly for the entire industry, suppliers and employees. in particular, i find the impact on staff redundancies unacceptable. therefore, the whole case must be properly investigated and the real culprits punished. i would like to emphasize again that this case is not a priori about intimidation or punishment, but about the awareness that by any kind of deception we are dealing with ourselves first. the eu must send a clear signal ahead of the upcoming climate summit in paris, where it is set to persuade other countries to make further environmental commitments, that it is capable of meeting its own commitments not just on paper but in practice.
in writing. i supported the joint motion for a resolution on emission measurements in the automotive sector because it responds appropriately to the unacceptable behaviour of some car manufacturers. the statement calls on companies to take full responsibility for their actions and to fully cooperate with the authorities in all investigations, and condemns the fact that many consumers have been misled by false information about the emissions produced by their vehicles. i personally requested that clear provisions be inserted to address the significant concerns about the potential impacts of the emissions allowance on the entire supply chain and the rank and file, and i welcome the fact that the resulting text is clear on these issues as well. on the contrary, i did not support several provisions which, in my view, are not based on demonstrable facts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on emissions from the automotive sector. i believe that in the future, practices such as the manipulation of software to circumvent emission limits should be avoided. i believe it is necessary to introduce new testing procedures. however, the process of introducing new procedures must be based on a realistic timetable for the transition from existing measurement methods to new ones, not only in terms of legislation but also with regard to the appropriate equipment of the approval and type-approval authorities. it is necessary to introduce a new test cycle based on measurement of emissions in real-use conditions. these measures are intended, in particular, to ensure a level playing field for all operators operating in the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed this resolution which strongly condemns the fraud by volkswagen, in which the company admitted to having installed defeat devices in at least 11 million of the diesel vehicles it has sold worldwide. the resolution urges the company to take responsibility and fully cooperate with the authorities in the investigations. it expresses disappointment that it was the usa who first found out and that the eu lacks enforcement of its internal market regulation. the resolution calls on the commission to launch immediately an investigation into the use of defeat devices as regards both the pollutant limit values and advertised co2 g/km. furthermore, it urges the commission to adopt and implement the new real driving emissions test cycle for all pollutants without any further delay and to bring it into force for regulatory purposes within six months. seeking to restore the confidence of consumers, it calls for the establishment of eu-level surveillance.

in writing. voting on the eu budget is one of the european parliament's most responsible tasks, as parliament has the final say on the eu budget. the adopted proposal will now be the subject of a conciliation procedure with the european council, followed by the final adoption of the compromise proposal at the november plenary. i supported all the sensible proposals that led to the avoidance of wasteful spending, such as the one on the ep's single seat in brussels, which would save millions of euros paid for moving permanently between brussels and strasbourg. on the contrary, money must be added where it is needed, notably to tackle the migration crisis at the moment, but also to support employment in the eu, especially for young people. the parliament thus allocated eur 1.16 billion more to supporting the management of migration than in the commission's original proposal. eu sanctions against russia help to fulfil the eu's strategic objectives, however, i consider it important that the eu is able to address the impact of these sanctions on its own most affected sectors. i therefore supported the proposal to increase the budgetary chapter for farmers whose existence is threatened by the reciprocal ban on food imports into russia. lastly, as a member of the itre committee, i am pleased with the increase in the budget for horizon 2020, as we fought hard in the committee to ensure that this programme did not lose important financial flows to finance the juncker investment plan.
