in writing. i did not support the increase of 28 judges to the general court, i.e. to double the number, because i am convinced, on the basis of the statistical data available, that such a increase is far in excess of the actual needs of the general court. i do not question the need for reform of the court as such, but i reject doubling the number of judges simply because the member states have not been able to agree on a rotation mechanism in addition to the realistic and corresponding increase in the agenda of 12 judges. i am generally not in favour of solutions that are inefficient, and this is unfortunately one of them, and it is not good for the citizens' trust in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted to change the status of the court of justice of the european union. this change will allow each member state to have a second judge. the increase in the number of judges will enable us to reduce the overload of cases per judge and thus also to reduce the length of proceedings, which currently amounts to five years, considerably. this will enable the european union to reduce costs, such as compensating the parties for the dispute's unreasonably long litigation. the czech republic is committed to the principle of equal representation of countries in the institutions of the european parliament. this change will enable the general court to better cover the different legal cultures that exist across the member states of the union. the increase in the number of judges will make the work of the tribunal more effective.
in writing. ‒ the i could not support the draft regulation amending the statute of the court of justice in relation to the general court for political reasons as well as legal reasons which i shall not mention here. the court of justice should be strengthened slightly because there has been a certain increase in the scope of the council's position at first reading, which was also agreed by the european parliament in 2014, namely the strengthening of 12 judges. 28 judges is too many, 1 judge costs european taxpayers just under eur 1 billion a year. the only reason for increasing the number of judges of the general court by 28 instead of 12 is that the member states in the council were unable to agree on a rotation mechanism. however, such a rotation mechanism could be found among the 11 advocates-general of the court. so this is a failure of the council, which is to be paid for by the taxpayers. the proposal contains in point 8a of the preamble support for the idea of the objective of gender balance among judges, which objective means that specific candidates will be subject to discrimination on the basis of sex, and therefore i cannot agree with it. moreover, such an objective will cause difficulties, especially in smaller member states. we need the best judges for europe, regardless of their gender. the reform was intended to ensure the proper functioning of the court in the changed circumstances. however, there are no arguments for increasing the number of judges by 16 more than the court of first instance originally requested.
in writing. ‒ parliament has approved a reform of the eu general court, doubling the current number of its judges. reforming the court, which is part of the european court of justice, is necessary in order to respond better to the permanent increase in the number of cases. however, the increase in the number of judges by 28 was motivated by eu member states’ interests in wishing to have as many judges as other countries. taking this into consideration, i opposed the increase for budgetary reasons and because the proposal makes no provision for a proper impact assessment.
in writing. - i did not vote in favour of increasing the number of judges of the general court by 12 as proposed in this report. i consider that this increase is not necessary, it would not lead to greater efficiency and would not speed up the processing of cases. the fact that the member states are unable to agree on a workable rotation system cannot, after all, justify the court having 28 judges.
in writing. ‒ i supported the approval of this resolution which seeks to amend regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 on certain provisions for fishing in the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) agreement area. in adopting it, parliament and the council agreed on the transposition into eu law of several recommendations made by the gfcm agreement. this will provide an appropriate framework for multilateral cooperation, focused on promoting the development, conservation, rational management and best utilisation of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea at sustainable levels and at low risk of collapse. the resolution also includes a statement on granting derogations to member states for the use of trawl nets and gill-net fisheries in the black sea.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this proposal. while i believe it should be for each member state to decide if it wishes to allow gmos to be grown on its soil, i cannot support a measure that would damage the functioning of the single market and which could set the precedent of allowing for the reintroduction of non-tariff barriers within the union itself. the commission should withdraw this proposal.
in writing. i voted against the proposal to allow member states to unilaterally restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food or feed authorised at eu level on their territory. i had several reasons for this attitude. firstly, it would create a barrier that could endanger the internal market; secondly, it would be virtually unenforceable, since the principle of free movement of goods within the eu implies the absence of internal borders and therefore of border controls; and thirdly, it would threaten the development of agriculture, which is heavily dependent on the import of genetically modified feed such as soybeans. lastly, the legal uncertainty of the concept of 'use' would result in legal uncertainty for the parties concerned. i do not think that consumer health protection is a valid argument either, because genetically modified food is not available on the european market.
in writing. as a member of the european socialist group, i naturally do not want the cultivation and distribution of genetically modified food to spread throughout the eu, where 60% of the population believe that gmos are harmful and dangerous for the future. but the legislation in question must be worked out with the utmost precision. the current proposal, on the other hand, was poorly conceived overall and needs to be reworked. the right to ban or restrict gmos already exists in the case of the cultivation of these crops, but this is necessarily limited to the territory of that state. on the other hand, a sales ban could lead to the introduction of additional border controls or an overall restriction of cross-border trade. in the document discussed, the commission did not put forward any plan to preserve the sovereign right of states to approach the issue without the consequence of adversely affecting imports and the internal market. the commission's planned procedure of agreeing on the existing proposal directly with the member states should not be accepted by them. a new proposal ensuring the safe and efficient functioning of the single internal market must be submitted.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal of the european parliament and the council on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. in my view, it should be for the state to decide on its territory whether to use the feed or food so modified. it is therefore easy for the european parliament to support this proposal and thus give room to the member states of the union in this area. however, even these measures must be compatible with the internal market and international obligations, such as those towards the world trade organisation. the measures taken by the states must be justified and supported by the relevant grounds and, of course, must be proportionate and non-discriminatory. i believe that this proposal will lead to greater satisfaction for the member states, because they will be able to regulate the use of genetically modified food and feed on their own territory.
in writing. ‒ today, all genetically modified organisms need authorisation before they can be placed on the eu market. however, a qualified majority among the member states has never been reached either in favour of or against any authorisation proposal put forward by the commission. the commission has therefore concluded that the legal framework for decision making on genetically modified (gm) food and feed needs to be adapted. the member states would thus be allowed to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory, despite it being authorised at eu level. i voted in favour of amendment 1 calling for the rejection of the commission’s proposal. by this vote i expressed my serious concerns about the proposal. the commission proposed more flexibility for the member states to limit or ban the use of gm food and feed on their territory. under this regulation, member states could block the free circulation of feed, which would have a negative impact on the internal market (in violation of article 34 tfeu).
in writing. i supported the agreement reached by the ep and the council at first reading because i believe it is the right response to technological progress, which has led to the emergence and development of many innovative new foods that are not regulated by the current regulation. i see the benefits of introducing a centralised authorisation procedure for novel foods in the eu, which should lead to a reduction in the costs of the authorisation procedure. the current widespread practice of double-checking means an average cost of between eur 20 000 and eur 45 000, which is a considerable burden, and unnecessarily high, for smes in particular.
in writing. ‒ to keep up with technological development and innovation, the eu considered it necessary to update the rules on novel foods. the current legislation dates back to 1997, therefore food and food ingredients which were not consumed in the eu to a significant degree before the entry into force of the current regulation are considered to be ‘novel’. the commission’s proposal from december 2013 brought several changes compared to the 1997 regulation (e.g. a centralised authorisation process and the removal of specific categories of food from the scope of the regulation). the agreement with council brought, for instance, improved transparency in the applications system, the re-introduction of the food categories in updated form and some new categories as well as safety assessment using the most up-to-date test methods. given the length and complexity of the examination of the draft regulation on novel foods, i support the agreement reached with council as an acceptable compromise and i hope for the swift implementation of the new rules.
in writing. ‒ in december 2013 the commission presented a proposal on the directive on national emissions reduction commitments. despite improvements in air quality in the eu in recent decades, we are still far from achieving the quality levels we need. the commission proposed a number of annual reduction objectives for several pollutants (including the transposition of the gothenburg protocol, 2025 indicative targets and 2030 binding targets, aimed at achieving 70% of the ‘maximum technically feasible reduction’ identified in an impact assessment) as well as the addition of pm2,5 and methane to the list of pollutants. while i am very much in favour of limiting air pollution, in order to protect the health of eu citizens and the environment, i am opposed to strengthening the reduction targets and making the intermediate 2025 targets binding. i voted in favour of the deletion of methane and mercury from the scope of the directive and i voted against higher reduction targets proposed by the committee on environment, public health and food safety, as these could have a significant impact on eu industry. the higher targets for 2030 were voted down; the inclusion of methane and ammonia and the binding 2025 targets were approved. therefore i decided to abstain in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ this scandal has highlighted a fundamental flaw in the introduction of any new measures. in this particular case of emission measurements in the automotive sector, the question of whether it is realistic to achieve these values and how they can be enforced, if any, should have been examined from the outset. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european commission should take a closer look at this scandal and, above all, review the current measures.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the european citizens' initiative, which i consider to be an important tool for citizens' participation in the eu decision-making process. the commission should review the wording of article 10 (c) of regulation no 211/2011 in this context, in order to ensure a proper follow-up to a successful european citizens' initiative, including a debate on the european citizens' initiative in parliament's plenary and a subsequent vote. it would also help to improve the functioning of this instrument if the commission started preparing a legal act on successful european citizens' initiatives within 12 months of receiving them. these changes could help to increase citizens' confidence in the eu and its decision-making processes.
‒ the european citizens' initiative is the first tool to allow citizens to participate directly in shaping european policies and legislation by inviting the european commission to prepare a specific legislative proposal (the initiative must have the support of at least 1 million citizens from at least 7 eu member states). it complements the right of citizens to petition parliament and to refer matters to the european ombudsman. as a social democrat, i am in favour of strengthening the elements of direct democracy, and therefore i very much welcome the existence of this possibility, as i see that much needs to be improved in this field. this is demonstrated by the fact that only three citizens' initiatives have reached the final stage since the launch of this option in 2012. the european parliament adopted a resolution in september on the first ever successful right2water initiative. at the october plenary i supported this report, which proposes a number of concrete improvements, for example on the online signature collection system and the overall simplification of the system (language support, contact points, etc.). i am very pleased that the report includes a call for the age limit to be lowered to 16. i believe that young people should be involved in public life as early as possible and i regularly assure them during my regular meetings with secondary school students that they often follow events in the european union with great attention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a european citizens' initiative tabled by my colleague from the committee on petitions. this proposal will be a tool for all citizens of the european union who wish to participate in the launching of legislative initiatives. it is desirable that citizens themselves should be involved in the running of the union. i therefore welcome this proposal and i hope it will help people with initiative to enter into democratic discussions. it is the first instrument of participatory democracy in the european union where an initiative can be launched on the basis of one million signatures from at least one quarter of the member states. it's clear that active people want to express their opinions. in my view, they should therefore be able to participate in the initiation of legislative proposals. i believe this change will have a positive impact on the field of citizens' initiative.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative is a tool to give european citizens the opportunity to participate in the launching of legislative initiatives. it has the potential to strengthen civil society activities and the concept of european citizenship, in particular at transnational level. since the launch of this option, 51 such initiatives have been launched by european citizens. none of them led to the creation of new legislation. i therefore supported the report, which gives a detailed assessment of the experience of the european citizens' initiative so far.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european citizens' initiative (eci) report because i consider this instrument of european citizens' participation in the eu public sphere to be very important and beneficial. it is a tool for all eu citizens, who can launch their initiative in different member states at once and thus highlight areas or problems that require new legislative action. as soon as the eoi regulation entered into force, it became clear that this was a tool that the public wanted to use. unfortunately, over time, the process has also proved to be unnecessarily complex, imposing unnecessary demands on the initiators of the initiative, and a number of rules governing the process are not clearly defined. the european parliament now intends to draw attention to these problems and call for their correction. breaking the european commission's exclusivity for legislative initiative seems too revolutionary a demand at the moment, but i am convinced that the eoi can still be a meaningful and useful tool if existing shortcomings are addressed and the eoi becomes more user-friendly. the ep's role in this process is irreplaceable, as it is the only eu body that directly represents the citizens of the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i share the view that the functioning of the european citizens’ initiative (eci) needs improving. the report aims to make it more user-friendly and to eliminate some of the obstacles that complicate organising an initiative. the eci has been in place since 1 april 2012, and throughout those three years the commission has noted 51 initiatives, only three of which were deemed admissible. none of them has yet been followed by legislation – a situation that points to weaknesses in the instrument in its current form. the purpose of the eci is to give european citizens the opportunity to participate in launching legislative initiatives. amending it should enhance the mobilisation of civil society and facilitate the process of organising initiatives.
‒ in the current security situation in europe, it is more important than ever that the eu works closely with its immediate neighbours to tackle regional problems. the european union's strategy for the adriatic and ionian region will be very useful in this respect, which is why i voted in favour of it. from the security perspective, the key aspect of this strategy is to support the diversification of the eu's energy resources. russian aggression against other sovereign states in europe means that the eu cannot afford to rely on russia as its main gas supplier. russia regularly exploits the eu's dependence on its resources and blackmails the eu's eastern states by raising prices and suspending supplies. it is therefore important to support projects such as the ionian-adriatic pipeline, which will bring gas from the caucasus through turkey, as part of the eusair strategy. not only will this reduce our dependence on russia, but it will also increase cooperation with the caucasus states, which are not protected by nato against russia and need our support. eusair can also serve as an inspiration for similar regional cooperation projects in risk areas such as the caucasus in the future, bringing its states closer to eu membership.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report that scrutinises the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region (eusair), introduced by the commission on 17 june 2014. it is a third macro-regional eu strategy, together with the one for the baltic sea region and for the danube region. the eusair covers eu member states (croatia, greece, italy and slovenia) and non-eu countries, all of which have either ‘candidate’ (albania, montenegro and serbia) or ‘potential candidate’ membership status (bosnia and herzegovina). the aim of the strategy is to foster mutual cooperation among the countries and pursue their prosperity and sustainable development. the report sets out priorities in the fields of blue growth focusing on marine governance; regional interconnectedness, mainly in terms of transport and energy; quality of environment; and tourism.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is paramount to the success of the european union, and the europe 2020 strategy is a helpful tool to continue making the eu better. i would like to reiterate that this tool is a long term growth and jobs strategy to help push the eu forward in terms of employment, innovation, climate change and energy sustainability, education, and fighting poverty and social exclusion. i would also like to point out that although the broad strokes have been agreed upon, the implementation is still in the early stages due to some delays. i would like to stress that we cannot afford any more delays with a topic as important as this one. i believe that by working together we can ensure full coherence and synergy between all instruments within the eu.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed adoption of this report, which is the first european parliament’s report on the mid-term review of the europe 2020 strategy, focusing especially on the cohesion policy dimension of it. with a budget of eur 351.8 billion until the end of 2020, the cohesion policy is the eu’s main investment growth and development policy and it is therefore important to examine it rigorously. based on the review, the commission is expected to submit by the end of 2015 its proposals for developing it further. in this report, parliament calls on the commission to provide information on the concrete contribution made to the europe 2020 objectives by cohesion policy and demands that the review is focused on better interlinking the strategy’s five objectives. it also notes the importance of the new eu investment instrument, the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), which will support the mobilisation of up to eur 315 billion in investments and regrets that it is not clearly linked to the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which comes in response to the commission guidelines on the application of the measures linking effectiveness of the european structural and investment funds to sound economic governance according to article 23 of regulation (eu) 1303/2013 on the common provisions (the cpr). the guidelines pertain to a reprogramming and a suspension of payments which are not compulsory. the report states that the achievement of the esi funds’ policy objectives should not be hindered by the economic governance mechanisms and that article 23 of the cpr should only be used as a last resort to contribute to an efficient implementation of the esi funds. therefore, the report calls on the commission to deliver a comprehensive analysis of all available options other than the application of article 23 cpr to address issues that may trigger a reprogramming request.

about 20% of europeans suffer from health problems due to the change in time, while the remaining 80% cannot understand that it can cause problems for someone. health problems range from fatigue, drowsiness, and disorientation to digestive disorders, migraines, and depression, to triggering genetic diseases such as obesity and diabetes, as well as heart attacks. for people with autism, this change presents major problems. the direct and indirect costs of health consequences in the eu have been estimated by this research to be as high as a staggering €131 billion. this may mean that eu citizens spend almost as much about eur 140 billion per year on the eu as on the health damage caused by this single directive. the commission's reaction to that public hearing was a press statement stating that the member states had no complaints and that the commission would not deal with such a trifle. the commission therefore considers the health problems of one fifth of europeans to be insignificant. if the research of the 9 universities is correct, then the commission also considers the health damage to the union budget to be a trifle. i find such a statement scandalous. member in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims at establishing a european union agency for law enforcement training (cepol). cepol, the abbreviation for european police college, is the agency responsible for law enforcement training. it has a budget of around eur 8.5 million and its courses are mainly implemented by national police training colleges. the proposed regulation modernises cepol’s legal basis, brings it in line with the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty and entrusts cepol with the implementation of the principles of the new law enforcement training scheme proposed by the commission in march 2013. i welcome this proposal, since better trained staff can make a bigger contribution to fighting serious and organised cross-border crime.
in writing. the report on the draft regulation on reporting and transparency in funding transactions follows the green paper and the shadow banking communication published by the commission in 2012 and 2013. the complex and opaque nature of sfts makes it difficult to identify the counterparties and to monitor the concentration of risks. i therefore appreciate that the proposed regulation aims to limit shadow banking and to identify the risks arising from sfts, thereby contributing to the transparency of sft markets and thus of the financial system as a whole. the need for such regulation is also triggered by the fact that, following the structural reform of the union banking sector, activities currently carried out by traditional banks could be shifted to the shadow banking sector.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report as a way to enhance financial stability in the eu by increasing transparency of activities that qualify as shadow banking. the commission proposal focuses in particular on securities financing transactions (sfts) that comprise a variety of secured transactions with similar economic effects to lending or borrowing securities and commodities and to repurchase or reverse repurchase transactions. the regulation introduces three main measures to improve transparency: monitoring of the build-up of systemic risks; disclosing information to the investors; and setting minimum conditions to be met by the parties involved. an important feature of the draft regulation is that it fosters financial stability without putting an additional administrative burden on the management of funds that channel money into the real economy.

in writing. ‒ the long-term unemployment rate differs greatly from one member state to the other. in czech republic, where the unemployment rate is one of the lowest in the eu, it currently reaches 2.3 %. the most important element in fighting the long-term unemployment is to maintain the skills of the jobseeker. we need to focus on the jobseeker’s continuous education and reskilling in order to match his or her skills and qualifications to the demand on the labour market. with this resolution, parliament has made an innovative proposal to the member states to be able to tackle long-term unemployment across europe and i fully support it. it suggests an individual approach towards long-term jobseekers through a ‘job integration agreement’, stipulated between the jobseeker and employment services. such agreement would assess the individual’s potential and suggest the approach to be taken for his or her reintegration at the labour market before reaching 18 months of unemployment. i urge the member states to commit to this recommendation for the sake of a competitive europe with a dynamic labour market.

in writing. ‒ rpas are being developed and operated all over the world, and europe is currently home to the largest number of civilian operators. i am glad that parliament has taken on this issue because rpas are surely going to be more prevalent in the future, and we need to ensure that their use is safe for their operators as well as other manned and unmanned aircraft. some of the key issues are: whether there should be a distinction between professional and recreational use; the question of out of sight flights; and areas where operation would be considered unsafe. these are only some of the hurdles that must be tackled and more will present themselves as we go further down this road. however, i believe it is necessary that we start taking on these issues early because rpas are here to stay and can be useful for industries, as well as recreation.

in writing. i voted for the report on the safe use of remotely piloted aircraft systems (rpas), commonly known as drones. this ep report concerns drones used in civil aviation. this technology was originally developed for military purposes but is now beginning to benefit various civilian applications, whose added value increases with the increasing distance between the machine and the pilot controlling the machine remotely. the report furthermore rightly emphasises the need to put in place appropriate policies to protect privacy and address safety issues related to the operation of drones. it is also necessary to establish a clear european legal framework to ensure investment and the development of a competitive european rpas industry. the development of appropriate innovative technologies is necessary for the full integration of rpas into european airspace.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report which sets the first step towards a european framework for the safe use of drones. drones are a new and popular technology which is developing extremely fast. whether it is for leisure or for professional purposes, drones bring enormous opportunities that should not be hampered, therefore the regulators, the industry and commercial operators must work together. the many benefits we can derive from the use of drones dwell in the fact that they operate in the airspace; this is also the reason why their use must be carefully examined so that an unexperienced pilot cannot threaten the activities of the other users of the airspace such as flights or emergency air services. that is why i support a clear european framework which should be elaborated on a risk-based approach and needs to take into account the characteristics of the drones e.g. weight, scope of operation or speed, but also the purpose of their use.

in writing. ‒ i consider it important that the european parliament has formulated and agreed a report on the new challenges and strategies in the field of tourism in europe, thus supporting the maintenance of europe's current position as the world's leading tourist destination. comprehensive support for the tourism sector, which generates 10% of eu gdp and employs 13 million workers, not only contributes to sustainable economic growth and employment, but also highlights europe's rich cultural diversity and strengthens european identity. i welcome the call to member states, regions and businesses to make systematic and as transparent as possible use of the new funding opportunities available through the eu's structural funds and programmes. improved coordination between member states, together with a greater involvement of digital infrastructure, is essential to further develop this key sector of the european economy. i therefore also welcome the initiative to establish a european year of tourism and to consider the establishment of a european tourism agency, which seeks to raise the profile of europe as a whole, with an emphasis on protecting the diversity and uniqueness of europe's regions.
in writing. i supported today's report on new challenges and strategies for promoting tourism in europe. i believe that it is absolutely right that the treaties do not allow for the adoption of uniform union legislation in the tourism sector, but i do recognise that some degree of cooperation, exchange of experience or also coordinated application of lessons learned from this experience is appropriate, since to some extent the european union as a whole is exposed to the competitive environment of other destinations in the world and this competitive environment needs to be addressed. the experience and improvements in digital services in tourism, for example, can then be used at the regional level, which is still the primary level and whose success is a prerequisite for a competitive european tourism policy.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report, which looks at possibilities for europe to better promote itself as a tourist destination. currently, europe is the world’s number one tourist destination and the majority of trips abroad by eu residents remain within the eu. tourism is extremely beneficial for the european economy and i think we could gain more of it if we, for instance, facilitate access to finance for companies working in this sector or encourage the digitalisation of our infrastructure. eu public money should be used for projects with clear european added value and so strengthen the development of cross—border tourism projects. in this respect, we should support the implementation of integrated and multimodal forms of transports which are strong incentives to cross-border tourism and a prerequisite for travelling.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe we do need a tracking system in all aircrafts. after the tragedy of malaysian airlines 370 and all the events before and since, there is no excuse for such a system not to be present. while radar is able to cover most flights, once a flight is out of range or over a sea, it is flying blind. i hope we will agree an international gps tracking protocol soon for all our safety.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a motion for a resolution supporting the commission's action to rapidly develop a more efficient global flight tracking system that will enable air navigation service providers to locate public transport aircraft at any time. i believe that the development of this system will promote better cooperation and coordination between all the actors concerned, such as the aviation industry, air carriers, air navigation service providers, safety and rescue services or international organisations. it is also necessary to ensure interoperability between alternative technologies in order to avoid disruption of airspace protection and security and to allocate an appropriate radio spectrum band to avoid any interference, in support of the future development of a global satellite flight tracking system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as it is more than timely that the eu works on the development of satellite-based flight tracking technology. the disappearance of air france flight af447 and malaysia airlines flight mh370 proved that the full coverage of airspace by tracking technologies is a matter of safety. today, only satellite technologies enable such a coverage, even above oceans, but to be fully operable they require a specific spectrum band. the allocation of spectrum bands will be discussed next month during the world radiocommunication conference.
in writing. ‒ after the malaysian airlines plane crash, it was very difficult and time-consuming to identify its location at all. that is why this resolution calling for the introduction of global surveillance of aircraft tracks, including over the sea and the ocean, is very important and i have supported it. it turns out that our current technology is not enough and we need to work on developing it.
mr president, i appreciate the fact that the commissioner appreciates the resolution. it looks, madam commissioner, as though we are heading in the same direction and there is a large degree of overlapping. i find the resolution is a balanced one. it is not perfect, but i think that we have set out the objectives. let me first reflect something that some of my colleagues have said. it seems to me that the fact that some airlines are not doing well is not the fault of the airlines or of the national member states. we always had the eu to blame for it. certainly we need an aviation package. clearly, we will have to address the burden. we will have to have a look at the internal market and we will have to have an equal level playing field, as you have said. if there is state aid somewhere, we have to address it. the commission will have to make the effort. but protectionism is not the way out. i do not think that this is what we should be doing. i must say, madam commissioner, that we are impatient too. we believe that if the seven points that we have outlined are well elaborated and developed, there would be a solid basis for our interaction. i am looking forward too, but i think that the principles should lead to real competitiveness and not just protection, and i am sure that we are on the same page on that.
mr. chairman, i'd also like to comment on the upcoming air package. most of us are well aware that the aviation market is one of the most liberalized markets in the world. the competition is huge. nor is it new that practices that lead to a weakening of social standards are taking place in the context of the acquisition of competitive advantages. this also applies to the current unsatisfactory situation of aircrew, which is also caused by a variety of atypical forms of employment. the social aspects of air travel really must not be underestimated. especially if they could affect traffic safety. the future of air passengers will depend first and foremost on their confidence in air safety.
mr president, zero rating is a honey trap for consumers, especially young consumers. while enjoying free access to some sites, they do not fully realise that they are being led down the path to a habit of spending all their money and data in that one place. it is creating a social addiction to one content provider over another. such practices are not new. there is no such thing as a free lunch. they have existed in the marketing world since the start of advertising. but just as we must control misleading practices in the physical world, we must be equally careful in the digital world. as the commissioner has just said, national authorities will have the power to prevent the misuse of such zero-rating practices. but, if they cannot prevent abuse, this should be part of any review of telecoms regulation. this is not only a question of defending the principles of net neutrality, but also of fair competition in the digital single market.
mr. chairman, i've listened with interest to the discussion and questions about what kind of internet we want or whether there should be a zero rate. i think that was actually answered in our previous resolutions on net neutrality. and i am a little surprised at my colleagues that they reject the zero rate, that they consider it inappropriate, that they want to decide in advance for the consumer without really having clearly demonstrated the negative effect. i don't know if we really want to literally guide consumers by the hand, predict their future in this way. i would also leave the responsibility to the market, which should not be interfered with at the outset, the market should be liberal, and the harmfulness of those effects must first be demonstrated and then can be interfered with. i am surprised that anyone would want to oppose zero interest rates in advance.

madam president, i would like to comment on the demands made by the british prime minister this week, which i believe are an attack on the fundamental principles of the eu. for me, as a citizen of the czech republic with our historical experience, restrictions on freedom of movement are unacceptable, even if they affect only parts of the member states, and perhaps that is precisely why. freedom of movement is one of the pillars on which the european union and its foundations are based. without these pillars, i believe that the union as such cannot continue to exist. the commission's proposal to limit social benefits for nationals of other member states is also economically unjustified. there are statistics and data showing that uk citizens benefit from the social welfare systems of other member states to a greater extent than citizens of other member states benefit from the uk social welfare system. i do not understand this request either, and i hope that it is not an ultimatum but a really rational and normal debate.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposed programme on interoperability solutions for european public administration as i find it essential to promote the digitalisation of public administration. it is one of the key features of the overall digital agenda to be developed throughout the eu. the czech republic has a poor record in this area and some serious effort must be made in order to modernise national public administration. the funds provided through the new isa2 instrument could be a very useful contribution to the government’s initiatives in this field.
in writing. ‒ while i see the potential benefits of interoperability, i see this legislation as an expensive eu programme to 'europeanize' public administration and take it out of national control, not as a tool for efficiency. that's why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a draft decision introducing an interoperability solution programme for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (isa). interoperability should in particular help to remove obstacles to the exercise of the rights of eu citizens. this is closely linked to the objective of introducing e-government, which should make it easier and simpler for citizens to communicate with public authorities. at the same time, however, attention must be drawn to the risks involved, such as the possibility of hacking the network, i.e. how to ensure the protection of personal data, often insufficient coverage, consideration for older citizens who already have difficulty learning to move and use digital devices, and therefore also the phenomenon of the potential emergence of new excluded groups of the population. the isa2 programme should also contribute to the achievement of those objectives. i consider the report to be balanced in that it also draws attention to possible risks, which is why i voted in favour in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ i supported the commission's proposal to establish an interoperability solution programme for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (isa2). i appreciate that isa2 represents a significant shift in focusing on businesses and citizens with the aim of modernising the public sector to respond more effectively to the needs of the public. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 concerning the conditions for the participation of third countries in union programmes. increasing interoperability means improving the quality of public services, which can benefit both businesses and citizens.
‒ i consider interoperability to be essential for maximising the social and economic potential of information and communication technologies and, as a result, only with sufficient interoperability will we be able to achieve the objectives of the european digital agenda. the eu will therefore put in place a new isa interoperability solution programme for the period 2016-2020, which builds on the previous programme, which expires at the end of this year. the eu has already done a lot in the area of interoperability, but there is still much work to be done to achieve the ideal state of digital connectivity between organisations, public administrations and citizens. lack of interoperability often constitutes an obstacle to the deployment of digital services between end-users and to the creation of single points of contact for businesses and citizens. maximising the interoperability of european institutions and public administrations is essential for the completion of the digital single market, which will allow citizens to fully benefit from interoperable electronic services, including e-government and e-health. i am convinced that interoperability is one of the policies that we can manage most effectively at european level. this requires a common concept of interoperability and an integrated solution. for citizens and businesses, better interoperability will mainly mean more efficient, simplified and user-friendly e-government.
in writing. i was happy to support the commission's proposal to set up an interoperability solution programme for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (isa2). this programme, which builds on the existing very successful isa1 programme, is a major step forward, mainly because it is newly targeted at businesses and citizens. considerable scope is thus given to the real needs of the public. in today's europe, more and more citizens are working and doing business across the eu and therefore need to communicate with public authorities. unfortunately, they very often encounter electronic administrative obstacles that prevent them from using public services effectively and, as a result, from the smooth functioning of the eu internal market. the interoperability solutions programme will contribute to the improvement of public services within the eu. it will lead to the proper implementation of a wide range of eu policies, for example in the areas of public procurement, health, taxation. it will ensure increased competitiveness and help deliver on the european digital agenda, all while benefiting businesses and citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (isa2): interoperability as a means of modernising the public sector. e—goverment solutions are becoming more and more important, or rather necessary. digital solutions in public administration can bring significant savings, make public administration easier and faster and ensure seamless electronic cross-border or cross-sector interaction between public administrations, businesses and citizens. therefore i support the isa2 programme – the follow-up programme to isa, which ran from 2010-2015. isa2 is expected to start on 1 january 2016, and to run until 31 december 2020. the new eur 131 million programme will support the development of interoperable digital solutions, which will be available to all interested public administrations in europe.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on the motion for a resolution on the reform of electoral legislation. it is a sad fact that the voter turnout in the european elections is also on a downward trend. nor did the news that the largest political groups are nominating a candidate for president of the european commission, which some politicians have promised will make the european elections more attractive. the resolution we are voting on today contains proposals with which i cannot identify, in particular the introduction of a single european candidate, whereby the whole of the eu would serve as one constituency. this reform would, of course, seriously harm small parties from small member states, whose chances of being elected would be practically nil. i also cannot agree with other proposals, such as the introduction of a single eu-wide election day, a single deadline for the submission of candidate lists, and the so-called european electoral commission. the adoption of these proposals would imply disproportionate interference with the constitutional legal traditions of the member states or would directly require amendments to the constitutions of the member states. that is why i voted against the motion for a resolution in the final vote.
in writing. i supported the report on the reform of the european union's electoral legislation, motivated by the desire to make the ep electoral system more transparent and 'european'. the council will now be in charge, but it is good that it has received the impetus, for example in the form of the requirement to ensure gender equality in the form of lists of candidates and to allow the introduction of electronic and internet voting and voting by correspondence, which would make it easier for citizens of the union, in particular those with reduced mobility or living abroad, to vote.
in writing. the declining voter turnout at a time when the european parliament's decisions are reflected in people's daily lives confirms the large communication gap between the eu apparatus and its citizens and therefore calls for a number of changes. it is difficult for eu citizens to find their way around the organisation of parliamentary political groups, and it is not easy to understand that it is membership of a particular political group that affects the ability of an individual member to promote his or her views. i therefore consider it a step in the right direction if the affiliation of a domestic political party to its european counterpart is already clearly indicated on the national ballot. i regret that not all the progressive proposals were adopted, in particular the measures on the balanced representation of women and men on the lists of candidates. on the basis of my practical experience of working in the european parliament, i am also in favour of the proposal to establish a minimum threshold for election, which has not yet been established in some member states and has led to fragmentation, and on the other hand, in the interests of equal opportunities, an upper threshold must also be established. i consider the establishment of a europe-wide threshold of between 3% and 5% to be quite adequate. i am strongly in favour of introducing the possibility of electronic voting. i now see this as an absolute necessity and believe that this step will support the introduction of electronic voting in national and regional elections.
in writing. - i supported the resolution on the reform of the electoral legislation, although i hope that the lowering of the voting age will not happen. i think it is important that the laws of the member states allow all those who wish to vote in the european elections to vote. i also think it is important that the elections are organised as efficiently as possible. the resolution called on the member states to introduce postal voting, to agree on the same date for elections, to ensure equal representation of women and men on the lists of candidates, and to amend their electoral laws so that there could be no two-state elections in the event of dual nationality. but i voted against the recommendation to lower the voting age to 16. i do not think it is appropriate to recommend harmonization to the member states in such a specific area, because the maturity of the electorate is a very important condition for responsible decision-making, and i think that everything has its time. the slim majority that decided on the recommendation points to the problematic nature of such a change.
in writing. the report on the reform of the electoral law of the european union attempts to harmonise certain electoral rules in the context of elections to the european parliament. harmonisation of elections to the european parliament in all member states could strengthen the political dimension of european integration and harmonise electoral conditions in all member states. i remember the elections to the ep, for which i was a candidate, but i could not vote because i was on a foreign trip in kiev at the time and the election to representative offices is not possible for czech citizens in the european elections. this reform is supposed to eliminate this electoral inequality. i supported the proposal as a whole, but took the liberty of objecting to the introduction of mandatory gender quotas for candidates from individual member states. i consider this step to be unnecessary in the sense that while i respect equality between men and women, that equality cannot be used for the purpose of forcibly highlighting women on the candidate list. i am also glad that the ppe rejected the proposal to unify the minimum voting age to 16. this step is an infringement of the constitutions of the nation states and it would be very difficult to reach a european consensus on this point. but even so, there are a lot of points of contention that will have to be agreed by the nation states.

in writing. a competitive aviation sector is important for the eu, both economically and socially. the aviation industry directly employs some 500 000 eu citizens. the high level of competition in this industry over the last few years has led to a radical reduction in travel costs for an overwhelming number of eu citizens, which not only promotes tourism but also increases the level of european integration by encouraging personal contacts between eu citizens. it is therefore desirable to ensure that the aviation industry remains a growing and competitive sector of the eu economy. the strategy for increasing competitiveness plays a major role in this proposal and i therefore support it. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question are compatible with the internal market. the eu must also help the european economy to be competitive internationally. many countries, such as some gulf states, heavily subsidize and favor their national airlines, which then serve as a foreign policy tool of their governments. in the absence of similar support for european airlines, eu airlines are at a marked competitive disadvantage. it is therefore necessary to ensure a level playing field for this sector on the world market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's joint resolution on the forthcoming aviation package, because it is a set of measures in the field of aviation which should create better conditions for a more competitive european aviation sector and ensure both quality of service and the highest level of safety. consumers, airlines, airports and employees will thus benefit from new routes and airports, greater choice, lower prices and overall better quality of service and more job opportunities. it is also necessary to promote innovation in the field of air traffic control (atc) of remotely piloted aircraft systems (rpas), the use of alternative fuels, aircraft and engine design (higher efficiency, lower noise), airport safety (contactless solutions and one-off checks against unlawful acts), digitalisation and multimodal solutions (computer-controlled ground handling) and at the same time it is important to promote environmental protection, such as global market-based measures to reduce co2 emissions from international aviation.

madam president, this report on reducing child poverty, although it has no direct legislative implications, is undoubtedly a very strong appeal to the institutions of the european union and to the member states. i would like to thank mrs zuber for her very helpful approach to the amendments and for the consensus we have reached. the poverty of children is dependent on their families, on their parents. so the report also addresses families, better childcare, employment, affordable housing, affordable health care for families. the way out of poverty the way to a better prospect for children is to improve their education and especially their completion of secondary education. quality education is one of the main tools for reducing poverty. this also relates to the proposal for free meals, extracurricular services and extracurricular activities. i think it also has to do with dealing with the migration crisis and taking care of the children who come here.
in writing. one in four children in eu countries is now at risk of poverty. children of long-term unemployed parents, children of single mothers and children of immigrant families are also strongly represented in this category. child poverty thus becomes one of the indicators of the effectiveness, or rather the ineffectiveness, of integration policies. since the start of the economic crisis in 2008, the proportion of children living in poverty has increased quite significantly, even in those eu countries that are among the richest. the risk of poverty among children is also increasing in families where one or both breadwinners are dependent on part-time contracts. they are the fastest growing sectors of the labour market in recent years. the measures proposed by the rapporteur do not take account of the new situation created by the influx of refugees from disintegrated countries. it is to be expected that the risk factors of child poverty (unemployment, part-time work, incomplete families) will be particularly frequent among them. the measures proposed do not provide a good enough picture of how to tackle the integration of migrants without also affecting the chances of tackling child poverty among the categories of population covered by the report. for political reasons, it would not be prudent to ignore this call.

mr president, the energy union is primarily a matter of energy security. i have four such short notes. the first concerns the need to diversify resources. we cannot depend on a limited number of resources and we need to participate in the economic development of siberia together with the russian federation and eliminate dependence on politically unstable areas. the second point concerns nuclear energy. the energy security of the european union cannot be achieved without nuclear energy, and here we really need to do everything we can to increase the share of nuclear energy. the third point concerns interconnectivity. the gas crisis of 2009 showed how crucial this question is. the european union has not made much progress in this area and we really need to do everything we can to make progress in this area of interconnectivity. the fourth point concerns the storage tanks. you have to have a supply of energy resources for the time of a possible crisis, for the time of unforeseen events. that's the lesson of 2009.

in writing. ‒ in this report, which i supported, parliament gave its consent to an agreement between the european union and the commission for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) concerning the membership of the eu in the extended commission. the eu can thus become a full member of the ccsbt extended commission, replacing the status of cooperating non-member that it has had since 2006. the ccsbt is responsible for the management of southern bluefin tuna wherever it is to be found. this move should further the eu’s contribution to the sustainable management of marine resources and combat illegal and unregulated fishing.

mr president, i would like to point out that the crisis in the steel industry is undoubtedly linked to a number of market factors, such as overproduction, but i think it is important to emphasize again that it is also linked to non-market factors. and that's adhering to certain standards, whether it's worker protection, favorable working conditions, favorable environment. this means how well individual countries and individual manufacturers comply with the requirements to comply with environmental protection standards. protectionism, which means unlawful state support, these are all issues that are related to this topic, and i think we should not give up on them when we evaluate, for example, china as a country that adheres to these standards.

in writing. i voted for the draft budget for next year, which, at €155 billion, is the highest ever, because europe cannot afford to go any other way in the current situation. the migration and security crises facing the european union must be addressed with sufficient financial resources. that is why i supported increased funding for neighbourhood policy, foreign policy, development and humanitarian aid, and also the mobilisation of the €800 million flexibility instrument to help member states cope with migration waves. i also supported the necessary staffing and contributions to decentralised and executive agencies, which are in a worrying and unbalanced situation of overburden on the one hand and underfunding on the other. these are in particular eurojust, frontex, europol, the european medicines agency and the european chemicals agency. although migration and security policy are the most discussed topics at the moment, we must not forget the fragile economic situation in which the union and its member states find themselves. the european union is experiencing economic growth, but its recovery is very slow and is driven mainly by exports. i therefore supported an increase of eur 53 million for the horizon 2020 science programme, the cosme sme support programme and the erasmus+ training programme.

in writing. ‒ i supported the objection requesting the rejection of the derogation for authorisation of dehp phthalate for recycling, as phthalates are substances harmful to human health and dehp is identified as a potential carcinogen. they can be easily replaced in production by safer materials. i therefore do not support their recycling and re-introduction on the european market.
in writing. ‒ phthalates that are hazardous to health should not pose a risk to consumers. but it's a technical question, not a political one, what is a dangerous phthalate.
in writing. i supported the objection to the authorisation of bis ((2-ethylhexyl) -phthalate (dehp). the reach regulation classifies this substance as a substance of very high concern, but allows its use subject to authorisation by the european commission, in close cooperation with the european chemicals agency. the applications which were the subject of the objection vote complained that the definition of industrial use was too broad, so that it was not possible to carry out a reliable risk analysis and exclude harmful effects. i concluded, along with most of my colleagues, that the applicants had not been able to demonstrate that they adequately controlled the risks associated with deph use. in my view, the granting of an authorisation would thus expose not only workers who come into contact with the substance to health risks, but potentially all citizens who may encounter the substance in everyday products.
in writing. ‒ i strongly support the european parliament's resolution urging the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision and to submit a new proposal rejecting applications for authorisation of the formulation of recycled softened pvc containing dehp. the european union must do everything it can to protect the health of its citizens. we cannot accept any compromise, we cannot succumb to the pressure of business in this respect, which sees the use of dehp through the lens of low production costs. dehp is contained in pvc and is commonly used in everyday products such as clothing, furniture and building materials. since it is not chemically bound to artificial materials, it is easily released into the environment. it is a 'reprotoxic' substance that disrupts the proper functioning of the hormonal system and is particularly dangerous for pregnant women. we must at least ensure that european products do not contain dehp. therefore, it is also necessary to establish clear rules for the recycling of such products, in particular for the recycling of plastics.
in writing. i supported the european parliament's call on the commission to withdraw the draft implementing decision in question and instead prohibit the recycling of plastics containing toxic dehp phthalate for reuse, as this toxic substance poses specific and publicly acknowledged health risks. nor should the idea of recycling materials, which i generally support, justify the continued use of substances with dangerous effects. i hope that the member states will join the european parliament in its position today and that the commission will reject the proposal for an application for authorisation of a formulation of recycled pvc containing dehp.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from voting on the european parliament's objection to the repeal of the exemption allowing the use of bis (2-ethylhexyl) -phthalate (dehp) in manufacturing and did not support the objection. my position was motivated by the clear opinion of the czech republic and also of the european commission, to which we entrusted the power to adopt sub-legal standards in this matter. at this stage, there are no serious grounds for prohibiting deph. on the contrary, such a move would harm producers who do not yet have a commercially acceptable alternative for this substance. it is clear, however, that in the future it is these very alternatives that need to be encouraged in order to end the deph exemption in the eu one day.
in writing. ‒ this report seeks to avert the commission’s proposal to authorise the recycling of old plastics containing diethylhexyl phthalate (dhep) into new pvc products. dhep is a softener banned by the eu’s reach regulation. there is scientific evidence that proves its negative impact on human health, especially its toxicity to male reproduction. deph is dangerous for workers that manufacture the products in which it can be found, such as textiles and furniture. moreover, it is not chemically bound to the plastic and can leak to the environment. i therefore supported the opinion that the commission should not allow the recycling of plastics that contain dhep.
in writing. a year after the luxleaks scandal was revealed, a report containing proposals for the european commission to tackle tax evasion and avoidance by multinational companies in the european union was presented to the european parliament's plenary. the controversial practices against which the ep has spoken are distorting competition in the internal market and reducing revenue for the state budget. among the actions discussed in the special committee on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect are the more efficient exchange of information between the tax authorities of the member states or the harmonisation of the method of calculating corporate tax (rather than the rate). as a member of the committee, i have been involved in this issue for a long time and have therefore supported this report.
in writing. i am against tax harmonization in the form of a common consolidated corporate tax base. the proposal 'promotes the speedy introduction of a full and mandatory common consolidated corporate income tax base'.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on tax rulings and related measures. it's been about a year since the luxleaks scandal, the special committee of inquiry in the european parliament. i supported the establishment of this committee as well as the extension of its mandate. statistics show that the eu loses €1 trillion a year in taxes, which is roughly equivalent to the annual gdp of spain, the eu's fifth largest economy. so this is an alarming number. i am convinced of the need for joint eu cooperation in this area. we need to work together to tackle tax evasion, tax fraud, tax havens and aggressive tax planning. the report also envisages the harmonisation of taxation and fiscal policies in the eu. i don't think the member states are ready for that. in my view, taxation and fiscal policy should remain the sole responsibility of the member states. that is why i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. i supported the report because i believe that the problem of tax rulings must be tackled, but i regret that the report has been infiltrated by a number of unfounded, irrational and dysfunctional proposals put forward by left-wing members, which unfortunately undermine the report's importance. examples include proposals to create new institutions, and thus new administrative burdens, in the form of a european body responsible for collecting sensitive commercial information and conducting investigations, or a pan-european whistleblower protection fund.
in writing. i voted for the report on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect, because i believe that tax fraud and aggressive tax planning must be stopped. in the european union, up to eur 1 trillion of potential tax revenues is lost annually through tax fraud, evasion and shadow economy activities. this situation is not acceptable and fair for ordinary citizens or smes. they are forced to bear the tax burden instead of large multinational corporations, which can circumvent regulations and avoid paying taxes through the current opaque systems. in particular, i supported mandatory and public country-by-country reporting. a system that would be available to tax authorities and contain more detailed information. he voted for greater coordination between the member states, whose competence is direct taxation, and which must establish a common framework and approach to find solutions to better connect where value is created and where profits are taxed. i also called on the commission to start working on the legal protection of whistleblowers, whose role was crucial in the luxleaks scandal. i also supported the commission's role in sanctioning member states and companies for engaging in and deliberately concealing harmful tax practices.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report that answers some of the questions that emerged in the wake of the luxleaks scandal. breaking out in november 2014, it revealed private tax arrangements between the luxembourg tax administration and more than 300 multinational corporations, which allowed them to achieve major tax reductions. the report makes several recommendations, based on the investigation by the european commission and by parliament’s special committee. following a critical overview of corporate tax practices in the member states, it calls on them to adopt concrete measures to prevent tax fraud. among them is simplification of tax systems, respect of the principle of profits taxation in the place they are generated, creation of an eu legislative framework for tax competition in the eu, coordination on advance tax rulings, increasing transparency by extensive country-by-country reporting system available to tax authorities.
in writing. ‒ i support the fight against tax evasion and i am aware of the need to expose and take the necessary measures against unfair tax practices by companies. it is, after all, one year since the luxleaks scandal broke, which exposed luxembourg's unfair tax-transfer practices, during the period when jean-claude juncker, the current president of the european commission, was finance minister and prime minister of luxembourg. it has helped companies avoid paying billions of euros in taxes and robbed us, the member states and eu citizens, of vast sums in the form of income tax deductions. however, the fight against tax evasion must not be used to further deepen eu integration, for example in the form of the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base, which is a risky step towards a single eu tax policy. member states must determine their own tax policy.

in writing. the fight against terrorism and the security of the citizens of the european union is a key priority for the european union in the wake of the recent attacks by the islamic state in paris. the report by ms dati is important for this fight, as it proposes concrete steps to prevent eu citizens from being radicalised and potentially involved in is structures. some of the measures i voted for include important measures to counter the ability of terrorist organisations to target eu citizens online and the reflection of this issue in schools.
in writing. i do not agree that there should be a harmonised approach to the definition of the offence of hate speech online and offline, whereby radicals incite others to disrespect and violate fundamental rights, and thus to include this particular offence in the relevant council framework decisions. the eu may want to apply this crime to hate speech and calls for violence by radical islamists, but it can be ambiguous and it can also affect critics of islam. in my judgment, only incitement to violence should be a criminal offense, but never the criticism or caricature of religion itself. i am against the introduction of 'educational programmes to mobilise, train and network young activists'. it is a completely misguided and desperate approach by the eu to the threat of terrorism.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on a very topical issue, the prevention of radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations. it's a very complicated subject. i agree with many of the points in the report, for example that we must fight the black market in arms, the black market in oil, which is a key source of income for terrorist organisations, and that those who have gone to syria or iraq to join or support terrorist organisations should not be allowed back into the eu. but then there are ideas in the report with which i cannot agree, such as the attempt to restrict the freedom of the internet altogether or the urgency of the passenger data directive. i also disagree with the fact that only the recent terrorist attack in paris is mentioned, but that the downing of a russian plane in sinai is no longer mentioned. i therefore could not support the report in its entirety and abstained in the final vote.
in writing. i supported the report by mrs dati, which i believe makes a useful contribution to solving the pressing problem of european security. i see its importance in that it correctly identifies the weaknesses of the current legal framework, which should be filled with high-quality legislation to combat effectively the threat of terrorism and other forms of serious crime. i consider it important, inter alia, to establish a common definition of 'foreign fighter' for the purpose of prosecuting persons who may be so designated. given the increasing activity of radical groups (not only islamists) on the internet, it is necessary to ensure stricter monitoring of hate-speech websites. in this respect, i have high hopes for the newly established internet content reporting unit within europol, whose task is to detect illegal content and also to support the member states in doing so. i think that a lower tolerance for these phenomena is a path to a gradual improvement in the situation today.
in writing. ‒ first and foremost i would like to say that terrorism cannot be associated with any specific religion, nationality or civilization. i also will echo the report by saying that unless the spread of terrorism can be addressed, the risk of eu citizens joining extremist groups and returning home is something that needs to be stopped. to this end the council should disclose its action plan and guidelines regarding the eu’s strategy for combatting recruitment and radicalisation. another area that this needs to be addressed in is in our prison system. in doing so, we must continue to fully respect the human rights if inmates. overall, to stop the spread of radicalisation we need to focus on the benefits of education and inclusion. with these aims we can help to end stem the flow of eu citizens to terrorist and extremist groups and promote peace.
in writing. the issue of preventing radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens into terrorist organisations would be important even if there were no wave of migration and terrorist attacks. the european parliament's report takes a comprehensive view and proposes solutions at both national and eu level. we must learn from the risks of a multicultural society, which are the ghettos, the excluded localities, the under-educated and unemployed generations of young people who have no prospects for life. the great risk is the spread of radical islam in mosques across europe, on the one hand, and the radicalization of anti-islamic militants within europe, on the other. in our report, we propose a number of practical measures to counter radicalisation in prisons, better control of the internet as a platform for the rapid spread of terrorist propaganda, better education and work with vulnerable young people and parents. we also need more effective work by europol and eurojust, or better linking of internal and external security instruments. but none of this will be enough if we continue to have a growing number of disillusioned and frustrated young people who are easy prey to radical ideology. the search for meaning in life is a human need, and it involves a spiritual need. europe is built on christian foundations and we should not abandon the spiritual riches of our predecessors. what we need is a combination of freedom and responsibility, solidarity and security.
in writing. i have today given my unequivocal support to the report on preventing radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens into terrorist organisations, partly because it brings new ideas which, if put into practice, will help to counter security threats on our territory. the report focuses on preventing terrorist radicalisation on the internet, as a significant part of the indoctrination and recruitment process takes place there. while i am a proud advocate of freedom of speech, i agree that there should be the possibility of taking legal action against internet companies that refuse to comply with a legal authority's requirement to remove illegal content from their internet platform, and that in the extreme case such actions can be considered as aiding and abetting comparable to criminal intent or negligence. after the recent attacks in paris, we must confront evil on all fronts, always with the rule of law at our side, but firmly and uncompromisingly. for the same reason, i supported the idea of harmonising the definition of a criminal offence for hate speech online and offline, whereby radicals incite others to disrespect and violate fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on occupational safety and health, a subject which, as a doctor, i have dealt with extensively, particularly during the last parliamentary term. it is clear that occupational accidents and diseases are a serious burden on society and must be prevented in such a way that workers enjoy good health and can work until a proper retirement. at the same time, new research on occupational diseases (e.g. the probability of developing different diseases by age group), psychosocial risks such as stress at work, the negative effects of certain substances such as asbestos or nanomaterials on human health, etc. should be addressed. the report therefore calls on the commission to develop an employment strategy covering all types of employment within the osh regulatory framework and to set indicative targets with the member states for reducing the number of occupational diseases and accidents, while respecting the latest peer-reviewed scientific evidence. i fully agree with the content of the report, which is why i voted in favour of it.
