for the group gue/ngl. mr president, a trade mark is a sign used to distinguish goods or services on the market. it helps us consumers to navigate more easily through the range of products and services and to choose according to our cherished wishes. union protection systems will operate alongside national protection systems. the systems will not compete, but complement each other, as we have proposed. we also have a better tool to fight against pirated, counterfeit goods. the undeniable advantage of a european trade mark is that, by registering a single trade mark, its proprietors obtain uniform legal protection for their trade mark throughout the european union. in addition to the increased legal certainty resulting from the single legal framework instead of the 28 different national frameworks, this brings about a substantial reduction in the costs of registration, maintenance of the marks in each country and the associated legal services. and it also makes the whole process cheaper for the individual applicant. i appreciate that we have been able to resolve a number of issues. i greatly appreciate the fruitful collaboration with all the shadow reporters, and cecilie, i want to thank you especially for the meds. thank you for your attention, and i wish you a merry christmas trademark.

madam president, i too would like to join in congratulating france and let us say not congratulating marie le pen on the way the elections have turned out. however, i would like to repeat what mrs šojdová said, namely the problem of linking cohesion policy with migration. i would like to say that for the first time we are hearing pro-european politicians from germany, austria and the netherlands linking this issue to the fact that if certain countries do not want to participate in the problems of migration, and i will not evaluate this, they will be cut in cohesion contributions, cohesion policy. i consider this linking of cohesion policy with the migration problem or the migration crisis to be a major problem in europe. i do not think we should be conditional beneficiaries of cohesion policy, of cohesion funds, but of course we must also show solidarity and i understand that, for example, cohesion policy could also be used precisely to integrate migrants. so i want to warn you about this.
madam president, let me start with the fact that the economic crisis highlighted a lot of gaps and problems in the architecture of monetary union, and we have been able to improve. we now have far better rules, better instruments and a better monetary union, and we should be proud of that. but what should we do now? obviously, we have a very good agenda before us and i am supporting that, but at the same time we should not forget that most of the work needs to be done by the member states. the member states should continue with structural reforms to improve their competitiveness, because that is the only way to deal with the issue of unemployment, which is very critical in most of the member states. at the same time, they should continue with responsible fiscal policy. there is no alternative to responsible fiscal policy, and these two goals do not exclude each other but, rather, are supportive. this is the only way to restore confidence – and i am talking about confidence among the member states and the self-confidence of the eurozone. this is what we badly need in order to move forward. member states ought to understand that, for the sake of a better future, they should be able to coordinate economic policies better and give up some economic sovereignty to make the eurozone more stable. i believe that the european parliament can assist in this development and play an important role.
in writing. while europe has bounced back from the economic bottom it was at just a few months ago, it is clear that the best solution has not been found. at present, our continent is facing considerable social divergence and a very low rate of economic recovery. the situation is not helped by the lagging domestic demand which needs to be stimulated. european citizens deserve their representatives to take action to reduce poverty and social inclusion. they also deserve to be stimulated by investments, including human capital and social investment. we must be able to exploit fully the potential that the juncker plan offers to the european economy. a plan that is currently experiencing a rocky start. the european commission and the european investment bank, which are responsible for the european fund for strategic investments, should reflect this and therefore seek to communicate as much as possible about the fund's capabilities. it is also important to stress that monetary policy is not a one-size-fits-all solution that europe can use to address all its economic ills. there must also be fiscal policy and counter-cyclical capacity. we must also remember that the completion of economic and monetary union is not just a matter for the euro area. since all member states have committed themselves to adopt the euro, with some exceptions, by the accession treaty, the debate on reform needs to be shared with all the members of the union.
in writing. i support the parliament's recommendation for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation on the modalities of the participation of the swiss confederation in the european asylum support office, as strengthening international cooperation between all european countries in times of an unprecedented refugee crisis is an indispensable part of the solution to the current situation.
in writing. ‒ i consider the full involvement of switzerland in the work of the european asylum support office to be very beneficial, especially in the light of the current situation. moreover, the involvement of switzerland is certainly a logical step in the context of switzerland's association with the so-called dublin system. i welcome the fact that switzerland will be able to contribute its expertise and the many years of experience it has in the field. switzerland, as a signatory to the agreement, will participate fully in the activities of the office from its entry into force, will be represented in the management structures of the office and will make an annual contribution to the budget of the office (a contribution calculated on the basis of the country's gdp).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report by which parliament gives its consent to the council to conclude the arrangement between the european union and the swiss confederation on the modalities of its participation in the european asylum support office (easo). the regulation establishing easo opened its membership also for iceland, liechtenstein, norway and switzerland as observers. according to the arrangement, switzerland will fully participate in the activities of easo, which i support, taking into account also its involvement in the dublin system. such enhanced cooperation can facilitate among other things the exchange of best practices, information gathering and early warning system.
in writing. ‒ i support this recommendation as it aims to involve switzerland more in the mechanisms to deal with the migration crisis. in my view, it is reasonable that switzerland, which benefits from the existence of the european union and the free trade area, should also contribute to the solution of the crisis. since switzerland has itself agreed to participate, there are no longer any major obstacles to its participation and i trust that the council will expedite its action as much as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of lifting the visa requirement for short stays for citizens of selected acp partner countries and the united arab emirates in the european union. this measure, which concerns exclusively safe countries with an excellent level of cooperation with european countries, will increase the interest of non-european tourists in visiting eu countries. the reciprocal abolition of the visa requirement for short stays will also make it much easier for union citizens to travel to those countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of concluding the agreement between the eu and the commonwealth of dominica on the short-stay visa waiver, which was signed in may 2015. it allows visa-free travel for eu citizens and for the citizens of the commonwealth of dominica when travelling to each other’s territory for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons, travelling for all kinds of purposes, except for the purpose of carrying out a paid activity. i welcome that the agreement strengthens relations between the eu and the commonwealth of dominica, which is significant in the context of the cotonou agreement. it is also another way of stepping up economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on various issues, including human rights.

in writing. i supported today's motion to approve the conclusion of agreements between the eu and several caribbean and pacific states on the short-stay visa waiver. it should be noted that the member states have already expressed their consent to the introduction of a visa-free regime for their nationals when they approved the mandate of the european commission to negotiate these visa-free agreements. the safety aspect has thus already been considered by the responsible authorities of the member states in particular. the list of countries whose citizens can travel to the eu without a visa is contained in the annex to regulation no 539/2001, and until now, the visa-free regime has generally been introduced by amending that annex. given that some member states may already have bilateral visa-free travel agreements from an earlier period and that these agreements may then make it more difficult to implement the basic rule allowing only 90 days in every 180 days to stay in the schengen area, it was decided to conclude, as part of the introduction of visa-free travel with third countries, union visa-free travel agreements which will clearly replace national visa-free travel agreements and reflect the 90 in 180 rule.

in writing. i voted in favour of the memorandum of understanding between the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim) and eurojust, as i believe that enhanced cooperation between these authorities, particularly in the area of enforcement of intellectual property rights, is necessary and can increase the effectiveness of not only these two institutions in this area. sharing information and experience across different institutions with interlinked agendas is certainly a step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of approving the conclusion of the memorandum of understanding between eurojust and the office for harmonization in the internal market. its aim has been to strengthen eurojust’s capacity to work with the office for harmonisation and foster their strategic cooperation, particularly on exchange of information. the arrangement is in line with eu legislation according to which eurojust may conclude agreements or working arrangements with the institutions, bodies and agencies set up by, or on the basis of, the treaties.
in writing. i supported the report on the methods and procedures for the allocation of own resources to the budget of the european union, because i am convinced of the need to introduce effective rules for the way in which member states pay their contributions to the common budget. only proper contribution can ensure the effective implementation of union policies that benefit half a billion citizens. i also supported the increase in late payment fees. i am convinced that changing the methods used to adjust the contributions of countries will avoid a repeat of the situation in 2014, when the method was recalculated, which meant that some countries increased their contributions by leaps and bounds. the whole process was accompanied by irrational anti-european comments which seriously and unfairly damaged the union in the eyes of the citizens. i also firmly believe that the european commission will look at how individual member states account for or report on contributions to the european budget and will seek to achieve harmonisation and increased transparency in this respect. it is time to reform the system of own resources of the european union budget. the current one is too complex and inflexible. it is not possible for member states, whose contribution is based on their gross domestic income and which account for the largest part of the resources of the european budget, to block the proper implementation of programmes which clearly have european added value by their negative attitude.
in writing. ‒ i supported amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 609/2014 on the methods and procedure for making available the traditional, vat and gni-based own resources and on the measures to meet cash requirements. according to it, the commission should be able to ask member states for the payment of 3/12th of vat and gni resources in the first half of the year, so that it can reduce a more important part of the previous year’s payment backlog in the european agriculture guarantee fund (eagf) and in the european structural and investment funds (esif), and to reduce default interest. among other things, the amendment aims at increasing the incentives for the member states to pay on time by making more expensive any late payment. it however respects proportionality, by capping the maximum increase of the interest rate at 20 percentage points.

in writing. ‒ finland submitted its application for a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in june 2015 in order to deal with redundancies in its information technology sector. finland argues that employment in its ict sector shrunk as a result of businesses and services relocating to china, india, taiwan and other non-european countries. while in 2008 the technology industry employed a total of 326 000 people in finland, the number of people employed by such companies in 2014 was 276 000. in 2014 alone, the number of staff in finnish ict companies was reduced by 3 % or 1 500 people. i supported the mobilisation of the fund, which will provide finland with eur 2 623 200. the contribution will be used to improve opportunities for the jobseekers to find new employment.
in writing. i supported the agreement reached by the ep and the council at second reading, which brings the legislative process to a close after two and a half years. the result is a compromise that simplifies the administrative process for processing trade mark applications and reduces the cost of obtaining a trade mark. the agreement will encourage firms to become more competitive in the eu internal market and thus promote cross-border trade within the eu. lastly, the agreement creates the conditions to facilitate the fight against counterfeiting in the eu and to reduce the volume of counterfeit goods moving through the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of amending the council regulation (ec) no 207/2009 on the community trade mark and commission regulation (ec) no 2868/95 implementing council regulation (ec) no 40/94 on the community trade mark, and repealing commission regulation (ec) no 2869/95 on the fees payable to the office for harmonization in the internal market (trade marks and designs). the purpose of these changes is to foster innovation and economic growth by making the eu trade mark registration systems more accessible, especially for small and middle size enterprises. the systems' efficiency should be enhanced among other measures by streamlining procedures to apply for and register a european trade mark, by increasing legal certainty and by promoting convergence of practices and developing common tools across the eu member states.
in writing. ‒ i have long been a supporter of measures to promote innovation and economic growth, and this proposed regulation is one of them. i am in favour of simplifying trademark registration procedures and thus increasing legal certainty. i also welcome the amendments to the proposal concerning the management of the office for harmonization and budgetary matters.
in writing. ‒ i supported adoption of this report as it foresees the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council to bring closer the laws of the member states relating to trade marks. i believe that increasing transparency and clarity of the procedures is crucial for supporting innovation and the development of european smes.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the effective functioning of pan-european corporations, which are one of the key elements of the european economy, requires the harmonisation of trade mark rules. the proposed directive, together with the community trade mark regulation, contributes to this and that is why i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which seeks the amendment of regulation (eu) no 1236/2010 of the european parliament and of the council laying down a scheme of control and enforcement applicable in the area covered by the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries. the convention, to which the eu is a party, aims to ensure the long-term conservation and optimum utilisation of the fishery resources of the north-east atlantic area. its commission (neafc) adopted the scheme of control and enforcement, which the regulation transposes into eu law. the purpose of the amendment is to implement several recent recommendations by the neafc amending the scheme. the main change, under neafc recommendation 9/2014, is the alignment of the scheme with the un food and agriculture organisation’s port state measures agreement.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the strategic cooperation in the fight against serious crime and terrorism between the united arab emirates and europol, and voted in favour of the cooperation. such agreements between europol and third countries have the objective of supporting and strengthening action by the competent authorities of the member states and their mutual cooperation in preventing and combating organised crime, terrorism and other forms of serious crime affecting two or more member states, and may concern the exchange of operational, strategic or technical information, including personal data and classified information.
in writing. ‒ i support cooperation with the united arab emirates as it would help to combat financial fraud, as this country is becoming a major hub for economic and financial crime. proceeds from criminal activities such as vat fraud and money laundering have been reinvested in the uae and key perpetrators involved in these frauds have taken refuge in the uae. such conduct must be firmly opposed.
mr president, it was important to me that this report was not militant, that it did not try to ban something which can actually bring about positive results in some areas. i don't want to question the environmental significance of scrapping, but there are areas where it can happen with relatively little impact on health and the environment. but as far as energy security is concerned, that is one of the european union's permanent tasks, and it is essential to me that the other european union procedures follow or fulfil the five pillars on which energy security must stand. it must be about secure energy supplies, and i insist that decarbonisation, a competitive economy and affordable energy sources must be an essential part of this. under these conditions, i will of course continue to support the creation of this energy union and energy security in the european union.
in writing. ‒ the energy market should be a full-fledged component of the eu internal market, fully functioning, competitive and secure. current fragmentation of national energy markets creates obstacles for more competitiveness and raises concerns over energy security in europe. for that reason i voted in favour of this report. on the other hand, i cannot agree with raising the energy efficiency targets high above the level agreed on the member states level which is, in my opinion, a well-balanced and realistic compromise.
in writing. the energy union project does not respect the individual energy needs of individual countries and, under the guise of solidarity, seeks to put some at a disadvantage.
‒ i supported the report because i believe that concrete steps must be taken to create an energy union, but that steps must not be taken that undermine this effort. for this reason, i have expressed my opposition to the proposed doubling of the nordstream pipeline capacity and, on the contrary, i am convinced of the need to find solutions that do not have a negative impact on energy security and diversification of supply. i would welcome the creation of a mechanism to strengthen the commission's role in negotiations concerning energy supply involving one or more member states and third countries, including the ex ante assessment of commercial contracts for gas supply. only a common approach to the negotiation of gas supply contracts can lead to a supply system that is profitable and sustainable for the eu as a whole.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the committee on industry, research and energy, i am very pleased that an important report on the energy union has been passed in the european parliament. european countries must move away from fossil fuel-based energy and move more progressively towards an efficient energy mix with respect for the environment and sustainable development. this, together with the requirement to integrate energy markets, increase security of supply and reduce consumption, forms the basis of the energy union, which should lead in the first instance to a reduction of energy import dependency. the energy union will not only help us to transform our economy into a greener, lower carbon economy, but will also have a positive impact on industry, transport, lower energy prices for households and consumer protection. it will also lead to the creation of new jobs.
in writing. i supported the report entitled 'towards a european energy union' because it addresses a number of specific aspects that are important for the implementation of the energy community reform towards the internal energy market and the so-called european energy union. in addition to the key themes of energy security, efficiency, support for research and innovation or investment in infrastructure, the report also highlights the social aspects of the energy market, including the consideration of end-users or the need to address energy poverty and the empowerment of vulnerable consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report ‘towards an european energy union’. the energy union is one of the most important projects which would, in the long run, ensure energy security and independence of the eu. the report calls for higher energy efficiency, increased use of renewables, diversification of supply, more active use of european energy resources, proper energy connectors between member states, renovation of infrastructure networks and buildings. of particular importance is to undertake further actions to build a fully integrated, synchronised and well-functioning internal energy market based on a market approach as well as solidarity and coordination mechanisms. i voted in favour of all compromises approved by the itre committee and i also voted in favour of those compromises concerning recognition of nuclear energy as one of the important contributors to the low-carbon european energy mix. i however did not support amendments calling for binding energy efficiency targets. i also voted against amendment 59 on shale gas.

in writing. i supported this report on my own initiative because interconnection of electricity networks is not only one of the essential conditions for completing the eu's integrated internal market for electricity, but will also contribute to meeting climate objectives and, last but not least, to enhancing energy security and stability in the event of disruptions to energy supplies. given the commission's estimate of eur 35 billion needed to reach the 10% target in all member states by 2020, the maximum use of eu financial instruments, in particular the connecting europe facility, part of which should be allocated to electricity projects, should be made. the funding should focus on projects that increase connectivity in the 12 member states in peripheral areas of the eu that are still below the 10% electricity interconnection target.

in writing. ‒ as a shadow rapporteur for the report ‘achieving the 10% electricity interconnection target’ i am deeply convinced that well-designed and functioning electricity interconnection is one of the key preconditions for completing an integrated internal electricity market in the eu. i consider the 10% interconnection target as a valuable step in this respect. therefore i supported all compromises approved by the itre committee and i voted in favour of the report. i would like to emphasize few points of this report which are of high importance to me. although the 10% interconnection target is important, it describes neither the quantity of electricity flowing between countries nor the quality, such as regards the availability of the existing interconnection infrastructure or of the existing national infrastructure. the report is therefore calling for thorough impact assessment and targets which will be evidence-based and also complementary regional targets in 2030 horizon. we should be able to identify the real needs of the market and needs of the eu member states, thorough ia and evaluation of the current infrastructure. last but not least, the approach towards the interconnections and the national grids has to be balanced.

in writing. from the social democrat's point of view, this is a very important instrument of microfinance, which allows reintegration into the labour market, unleashing entrepreneurial potential, acquiring new skills through accompanying vocational training and counselling, and enabling people to take their lives into their own hands and ensure a dignified existence. it is important to note that the progress microfinance facility is first and foremost a social policy instrument and only secondarily an economic instrument. it targets target groups that have been neglected in our economic system: the (long-term) unemployed, social welfare recipients, immigrants, ethnic minorities, people in the informal economy or living in disadvantaged regions, and women. in my view, the provision of micro-credit makes economic and social sense, because financial support for a person seeking to become self-employed is more advantageous for state institutions than social benefits for the unemployed, and moreover it serves as a springboard for citizens to start a business. moreover, the figures demonstrate the functionality of the instrument, which is why i would be happy to see the efsi made available to micro-enterprises.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report which stresses the importance of the progress microfinance facility. inspired by the success of microloans in developing countries, the eu created it in 2010 with total funding of eur 205 million and it currently operates in 22 out of the 28 member states. it is primarily a social policy instrument for a target group to which loans are considered risky and costly by banks. the report calls on the commission and the member states to raise awareness of the microfinance facility among potential beneficiaries, to encourage more research into microenterprises, their needs and their survival rates and to better measure the social impact of the facility.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the european commission has put forward a proposal to reform the common fisheries policy. the use and exploitation of our seas is in many ways a major problem that needs to be addressed urgently. current intensive fishing is causing the disappearance of entire species and the consequent instability of the marine and ocean biological environment, which is also affected by, among other things, climate fluctuations and changes. the 2013 cfp reform has made considerable progress, but there is still a need to improve and, above all, simplify measures in order to achieve maximum sustainable yield through an ecological approach. the new reform, which includes regulation of fishing effort, multiannual plans, regional cooperation and other technical measures, should ensure this combination. these measures should be adapted to each fishing area and region to the extent that they remain compatible with the cfp and thus the exclusive competence of the eu in the area of shared resources. the measures must be simple and clear, so that they are easily understood by fishermen and do not give rise to divergent interpretations. i think that the introduction of specific control standards to limit the exploitation of the seas is a necessary step that we must take now to avoid catastrophic consequences in the future.
in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of this own-initiative report regarding the common fisheries policy (cfp). to achieve the objectives resulting from its 2013 reform, technical measures and multiannual plans were identified as the two key instruments. however, little progress has been made and this report calls for improvements. it proposes that the multiannual plans should be adopted as soon as possible, involving stakeholders in their development. regarding the technical measures, it brings simplification and regionalisation. it calls for future technical measures to be clear so that they can be easily understood by fishermen and to include them in the decision-making process on the details of the technical measures.

rapporteur.– mr president, let me start by saying that it was a great pleasure to work with anneliese dodds and with all the other shadow rapporteurs on this fascinating economic and political subject, and on an area in which we can really make things better. anneliese dodds talked about the revenues lost by governments. we do not know exactly what they amount to: the estimates start at tens of billions of euros a year, but there may be hundreds of billions. in any case, it is a lot of money. an even more important issue is the fact that a market in which some companies pay taxes and some do not pay is not a fair market. we must address this issue. it is not a static issue: if we do not act, the situation will just get worse, and those who pay taxes, including employees and small businesses, will have to pay more because of the others who do not pay. this is an issue that has undermined the credibility of states and governments. so we must act. we must act decisively but we must act smartly: not everything that can be done should be done. luckily, there is enough expertise, on which we were able to build our report. i would mention the expertise of the commission and the oecd, academics, civil society and businesses. consequently, we have tried to put together the report with well defined, clear recommendations that are feasible and well justified. let me look at it from a different perspective. the first area i want to mention concerns implementation of the recommendations that were the outcome of the oecd/g20 base erosion and profit shifting (beps) project. the g20 and the commission asked the oecd to tackle this issue at global level. the results are well thought-out economic measures which have been endorsed by the governments of many countries. including the g20 and developing countries. there is no excuse for us not to implement these measures briskly. the measures concern, for example, country-by-country reporting, patent boxes, hybrid mismatches and permanent establishment. the second issue i want to highlight is the re-launch of the common consolidated corporate tax base project (ccctb). the ccctb project has benefits both for governments, as it will generate more secure revenue collection, and, importantly, for businesses because it will substantially reduce and simplify tax compliance. there is no alternative to ccctb if we want to tackle the issue. there is no other measure that would be as effective and as efficient at the end of the day. lastly, let me mention some proposals that are eu specific. we want a code of conduct group to function better. we want, effectively and jointly, to act against tax havens. there is the corporate social responsibility initiative that anneliese dodds mentioned and, last but not least, we want to work with regular estimates of the tax gap arising in the area of corporate taxation. i am very pleased that we are on the same wavelength as the commission because we have in mind the same proposals, and i believe we will be able to convince the governments to go forward. let me now conclude, first by thanking anneliese dodds for her wonderful cooperation, and all the shadow rapporteurs for their input. i look forward to the debate here and, more importantly, i believe we will gain support for the report tomorrow. i hope this is not the end. it is a start, and at the end of the day – though rather sooner than later – we will achieve the improvement that we want.
mr president, i would also like to highlight the quality of the report presented and thank the rapporteurs. i realize that this is a highly technical but also political question. i think it is obvious that certain aspects of taxation should be harmonised, they should be uniform. i don't think that's even the basic point of contention. however, i'm not sure that a common tax base should be the way forward for europe. i am aware that it is not possible to construct a european agreement in the absence of a global agreement, but what they have created in luxembourg and beyond, i think is really unfair tax competition. it is a practice that distorts the market, that is based on free will, and i think it is a blow to the other member states and to the citizens who believe in a common europe. i therefore support what has been said and i think it provides a good basis for further consideration.
rapporteur.– mr president, let me thank all colleagues for their kind words. after working for many months with anneliese i am not surprised that she made the same comment i would make concerning the remarks of some of my colleagues. as a former economist, i am sure that the current situation is not sustainable and i believe that no country is currently benefiting from the current situation or will benefit from it in the future. so we need a change. the questions are quite simple. do we want to allow some firms to benefit from very low effective taxation and ask others to pay in their place? do we want to allow some countries to redirect, intentionally or unintentionally, tax revenues from the budget of other countries to their budget? do we want to allow or encourage some firms to benefit from very low taxation, thus creating a tax advantage and unfair conditions on the market? i guess the answer is and should be ‘no’. i believe that we should allow countries to compete on taxation, but on fair and transparent grounds. we should aim for lower taxes, but lower taxes for everyone, not only for some. i hope that parliament will support the report tomorrow.

in writing. i supported the report on eu-china relations because it not only recalls the anniversary celebrations of the establishment of diplomatic relations and the importance of our strategic trade partnership, but also reminds china of the importance of effectively respecting its international commitments in the field of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the values of human rights, the rule of law and peace cannot be merely formally recognised by china, but must be reflected in its daily life. the widespread censorship of the internet, the religious repression of tibetans and uyghurs, and the marginalization of cultural rights of minorities in china cannot be easily ignored. the report's effort to recall china's role in international relations and as a permanent member of the un security council is also to be appreciated. instead of creating provocations in the south china sea and systematically blocking the un's work in the syrian conflict, china should make a greater contribution to peace and global security. i am glad that the report focuses on these questions. as a long-time advocate of ukraine, i also supported china's call to support us and eu initiatives aimed at ending violations of international law in the conflict in ukraine.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the relations between the eu and the people’s republic of china. indeed, this country is an important partner for some countries of the european union, but the relations are extremely unequal and more could be done to reinforce the link between the eu and china. in this respect the report addresses various different issues, such as the bilateral investment agreement currently being negotiated, the multiple meetings taking place between the two parties, respect for human rights, as well as china’s domestic and external policy.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on the preparations for the world humanitarian summit. humanitarian aid is a very important topic, so i'm glad we had the opportunity to discuss it. the report reveals the alarming fact that the number of people in need has more than doubled since 2004 and exceeds 100 million in 2015; 250 million people are affected by the humanitarian crisis; and the number of forcibly displaced people is the highest since world war ii, when it reached almost 60 million. we must also be aware that children, women and other particularly vulnerable groups are the most affected by these consequences. i fully agree that poverty and vulnerability to crises are inextricably linked, which underlines the need to address the underlying causes of crises and to meet the long-term needs of the population affected by crises. i am also very aware that the consequences of humanitarian crises will be even more serious if their root causes are not addressed and humanitarian aid is not better integrated into development cooperation. however, as the report emphasises the importance of the private sector, including commercial objectives, which i personally do not think is a priority in humanitarian aid, i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. i supported the report, which also contains some contentious points on cultural and ethical issues, because i believe that a positive signal should be sent to help make the forthcoming world humanitarian summit a success, based on impartial assistance and general agreement on the application of the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and respect for obligations under international humanitarian law.
in writing. ‒ the current complex international situation brings an unprecedented number of humanitarian challenges that require clear responses and a truly global and functioning humanitarian aid system. as a social democrat, i believe in the need to strengthen the system of protection of the most vulnerable, based on solidarity and shared responsibility. we need humanitarian aid to be more effective, more effective and more focused on prevention. at the world humanitarian summit in istanbul, turkey, in may, the current system should be significantly overhauled and strengthened. the european union is the largest donor of humanitarian aid, demonstrating, among other things, the strength of its values and its commitment to a truly global responsibility. i hope that the world humanitarian summit will bring concrete answers and improve the current situation.
in writing. i spoke to the plenary on this report and appreciated the many important information and recommendations it contains. unfortunately, it also contains a number of problematic points. among other things, it addresses issues such as abortion and reproductive and sexual health and rights, mentioning for example the guarantee of access to 'abortion services in humanitarian crises', which i personally find highly controversial. the attempt by my group to remove these items failed, so i eventually abstained, as did most of my colleagues from the ppe, in the final vote. in the end, the report was narrowly passed.
in writing. the continued increase in the number of humanitarian disasters in the world cannot be underestimated and there is a need to achieve gradual coordination of member states' policies in addressing the causes and consequences of such crises. in particular, i welcome the report's call for a stronger private-public partnership in developing strategies to prevent emergencies and disasters and to repair potential damage. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance in the context of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, in particular the countries of the former soviet union, the former soviet union and the former soviet union. the emphasis on the key role of ngos working in the field during humanitarian disasters and the need to consult them by national authorities can also be welcomed. however, i took the liberty of not agreeing to unconditional financial assistance and mandatory financial payments to governments, the private sector and regional organisations in addition to the funds for the planned global fund for humanitarian aid. i believe that the possibility for those entities to decide voluntarily to replenish the fund after a proper assessment of their own financial capabilities should not be denied. references to the question of abortion in the context of humanitarian crises also appear to be superfluous in the context of the report as a whole. in view of the above, i have therefore decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i endorsed adoption of this report in view of the world humanitarian summit (whs), which will be held in istanbul in may 2016 with the aim to adapt the humanitarian system to an unprecedented number of emergencies and to make humanitarian action more efficient and effective. the report notes that 250 million people are affected by humanitarian crises. it underlines that the whs outcome document should include a five-year roadmap for concrete political commitments undertaken, linking the post-2015 development agenda, the sendai framework for disaster risk reduction and the 2015 united nations climate change conference (cop 21). it suggests that one of the summit’s objectives should be to reflect on the need for un reform towards a transparent and effective coordination system. the eu, as the world’s largest humanitarian aid donor, should show leadership in the whs and urge prevention, as well as a stronger commitment to a human-rights-based approach in humanitarian action.
in writing. ‒ it is clear that the world faces a number of humanitarian disasters in terms of number, scale and duration. the number of people in need has doubled since 2004. i support this report because i believe that the european union, as a global actor with humanitarian values, must be present in this area and actively involved in providing assistance. these values should also be loudly heard at the world humanitarian summit in istanbul. i also think it is important to link the discussion of humanitarian aid with development aid, since one without the other is meaningless in the long term.

author.– mr president, the committee on legal affairs, which i have the honour of chairing, was in charge of directive 98/44 on the legal protection of biological inventions when it was adopted. the directive contains, inter alia, certain exclusions from patentability. article 4 of the directive excludes plant and animal varieties and essentially biological processes for the production of plants and animals from patentability provisions, reflected in the implementation regulation of the european patent convention. article 53b of the convention itself prohibits patents on plant varieties and on essentially biological processes for breeding. however, as a result of consecutive decisions by the european patent office (epo), the content of these exceptions has been eroded. parliament already adopted a resolution on this matter in 2012. unfortunately, it did not have much impact on the decisions of the patent office. in two precedent-setting decisions of march this year, the enlarged board of appeal of the office declared that, while processes for conventional breeding cannot be patented, plants and animals stemming from these processes are patentable. speaking on behalf of the committee responsible in this parliament for the application of eu law, i would like to emphasise the need to ensure that the epo demonstrates appropriate respect for eu law. the epo will play a central role in the implementation of the european patent with unitary effect. it is, therefore, worth bearing in mind that article 27c of the agreement on a unified patent court states that ‘the rights conferred by a patent shall not extend to […] the use of biological material for the purpose of breeding or discovering and developing other plant varieties’. i hope that this second attempt by this house to bring its concerns to the attention of the european patent office will help to convince the commission to raise the matter with the epo and will help to prevent, and possibly reverse, interpretations of law which erode carefully considered exceptions to patentability and patent protection.

in writing. i supported the report the ep adopts every year to draw attention to the problems of human rights violations in the world. the need for this year's report is all the more urgent as threats to human rights such as freedom of expression, freedom of thought, conscience and religion, and freedom of assembly and association are on the rise in many parts of the world, including authoritarian regimes, and attacks on human rights defenders are increasing worldwide. i did not support the point condemning the use of surrogacy and abstained in this case. i would not dare to say that surrogacy as such is a violation of the human dignity of women, since their bodies and reproductive functions are used as commodities and that it is reproductive exploitation. i can imagine situations where surrogacy is justified and morally justifiable, and i do not think it is appropriate to take such a categorical stance on this complex issue.
in writing. - it is important to me, ladies and gentlemen, that the report fundamentally denotes russia's aggression in ukraine. although it is said that human rights and pragmatism are two different lines that do not intersect, i have been convinced many times in my life that this statement is wrong. half-hearted approaches to human rights boomerang back, and the damage is often irreversible. for ten years, we have watched with little concern the decline of freedom of speech and freedom of thought in russia. during this time, the kremlin has controlled the media with highly sophisticated state propaganda based on half-truths, manipulation and lies. it misinforms not only the domestic audience but also the european and global audience with great success. the annexation of crimea, the russian aggression in eastern ukraine, the occupation of georgia, etc. the path to this aggressive foreign policy has been paved by the false manipulation of facts, the violation of freedom of speech, freedom of thought, freedom of speech and media in contemporary russia. let's try to make the kremlin look like a partner that won't be intimidated. 'violation of human rights cannot be the internal affair of any state,' said russian humanist sergei kovalyev.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world 2014 and the eu policy on the matter. the report calls on the european union to take ‘measures appropriate for tackling serious violations of human rights committed in third countries, particularly those by authoritarian regimes, as well as those in the field of trade relations, energy and security’. together with my colleagues we are calling on the eu and its member states to make more effort in ensuring that human rights and democratic values are ‘genuinely’ at the centre of their relations with the rest of the world and in all union external action measures, particularly those at a high political level.
in writing. ‒ the in the joint resolution we voted on today, we were left with the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace accords. it recalls that, although the agreement ended the war, it froze rather than resolved the conflict between serbs, croats and bosniaks in the country, and that ethnic differences persist within the political system established by the agreement and the decision-making process has become more complicated. so we acknowledge the successes on the one hand, but also recognize the lingering problems that exist in the country. the resolution calls on all parties concerned to engage in dialogue in order to achieve reconciliation. we also support bosnia and herzegovina in its efforts to achieve reforms in the light of a european perspective. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i consider it very important that the european parliament recalls the importance of the dayton agreement, which ended the conflict in bosnia and herzegovina a conflict that left a hundred thousand dead and millions displaced. the peace agreement laid the foundation for the post-war settlement, the division of power and the question of reconciling an ethnically divided population. it is clear that considerable efforts will still be required in this respect, for example, the implementation of the results of the seidić-finci judgment is not yet visible. it is also necessary to call for respect for human and civil rights and guarantee them to all citizens, and to encourage greater involvement of young people in democratic intercultural dialogue and political life in general. despite all the current problems, the dayton agreement set a clear direction for the peaceful development of bosnia and herzegovina. bosnia and herzegovina must now make substantial progress in the process of political reform and seek to move closer to the european union, where its future is unquestionably.
in writing. i was happy to support the european parliament's resolution on the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement. i personally welcome the fact that the resolution does more than simply recall the importance of the peace agreement which ended the bloodiest conflict in europe since the second world war 20 years ago. the dayton peace accords ended the war, but they did not resolve the conflict itself, and so it was more a preservation of the conflict. the introduction of an overly complex institutional framework has not brought the country the stability it needs. unfortunately, the ethnic and religious divisions of the country persist, with the potential for a resurgence and escalation of the conflict. bosnia and herzegovina has undoubtedly undergone significant change since the war and has managed to reach its current situation of aspiring to eu membership and of successfully coping with the problem of the return of refugees and internally displaced persons. the agenda is to implement constitutional and political reforms that will lead to the equal status and representation of the three constituent peoples of bosnia and herzegovina and their citizens. i am pleased that the resolution recalls and reaffirms the european union's commitment to bosnia and herzegovina's european perspective and its further rapprochement with the eu. a realistically defined european perspective for bosnia and herzegovina can also act as a significant motivating factor for reconciliation and overcoming internal divisions in the country.
in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of this resolution i call, together with my colleagues of the european parliament, on the authorities in bosnia and herzegovina to use the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement as an incentive to move forward with the necessary reforms, especially in view of bosnia and herzegovina’s forthcoming eu membership application. i note with regret that, 20 years after the end of the war, successive governments have failed to build a fully functioning, self-sustainable state. however, i recognise the positive transformation that bosnia and herzegovina has undergone in the past 20 years, from a war-torn country emerging from war to a state aspiring for membership of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i am convinced that especially at this particular time we have to make sure the rules on arms export are fully implemented and respected. on the other hand, i do not agree with the proposal to establish a european authority which would supervise the arms exports. there are national authorities which are doing this already now.
in writing. ‒ i am against the eu dealing with embargoes instead of national states.
in writing. in its report, the european parliament assesses the state of implementation of the council's common position establishing common rules on control of exports of military technology and equipment. the report, drawn up by mr kelam, the shadow rapporteur, was able to assess the security risks facing europe. the european union this summer lifted its arms embargo on ukraine, opening the way for ukraine to defend itself. in a situation where the minsk agreements are dead, it is the weapons that open the way to peace. no peace treaty with russia will guarantee peace. ukraine will have peace only if the aggressor is defeated. without weapons, wars are not won. another example is syria. the report refers to the decision of some member states to provide arms to iraqi kurds fighting in self-defence against da'esh. my country, the czech republic, has already delivered 500 tons of ammunition to erbil. defense against violence is the right of every free man, every free state. in wartime, you have to defend yourself with force. peace is an important commodity today. we have to keep asking how much does a kilogram of measurement cost in ukraine or syria. although the original draft report has been improved by a number of amendments, i am not satisfied with the content of the few articles in the original text that have not been removed from the report, nor with the overall wording of the report. i therefore voted against its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the implementation of the common position on arms export. the eu’s common position sets out the rules on monitoring the export of military technology and equipment. the member states undertook to comply with an eight-point code when selling arms. these relate, for example, to human rights in the country of final destination, the internal situation in the country of final destination, preserving regional peace, security and stability, and the potential effect on the economic and development prospects of the country of final destination.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint resolution as i am convinced that patent law should be duly implemented in the area of plant breeding, mainly in relation with the innovations in biotechnology.
in writing. the proposal is a response to the recent decision (g2/12 and g2/13) of the enlarged board of appeal of the european patent office, which allows the patenting of plant traits, even if these traits have been developed or obtained by means of essentially biological breeding methods. this decision is to be interpreted narrowly and thus opens up wide possibilities for the grant of patents covering plant varieties. this is in direct contradiction to the breeders' exemption explained in article 15 of the 1991 act of the international union for the protection of new varieties of plants (upov) and article 15 of regulation (ec) no 2100/94. i agree that if international obligations on intellectual property rights are to be met and if innovative competitiveness is to be increased within the european plant breeding sector, it is very important to balance eu legislation (in particular directive 98/44/ec). pursuant to rule 26 of the implementing regulation of the european patent office, directive 98/44/ec is to be used as a complementary means of interpretation for european patent applications and patents relating to biotechnological inventions. the clarification of directive 98/44/ec will have an immediate impact on the work of the european patent office. that is why i supported today's resolution.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support the resolution on patents and plant breeders' rights. the resolution calls for the prudent application of plant breeding patent law, which should apply to biotechnological inventions but not to the results of ordinary biological processes. i believe that the resolution is a correct call for restricting the patenting of plant traits when those traits have been developed or acquired by means of essentially biological breeding methods. i consider such patenting to be an excessive form of intellectual property protection which goes against innovation in the sector. i trust the epo will reconsider its decision. the resolution is also fully in line with the position of the ministry of agriculture of the czech republic. the text of the amendment, as drawn up by the agri and juri committees, is entirely sufficient and i therefore did not support the additional amendments tabled by the gue/ngl and the greens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the commission to urgently clarify the scope and interpretation of the 98/44/ec directive on patents, in order to ensure legal clarity regarding the prohibition of the patentability of products obtained from essentially biological processes, and to clarify that breeding with biological material falling under the scope of a patent is permitted. indeed, the recent decision of the enlarged board of appeal of the european patents office (epo) on cases g2/12 (tomatoes) and g2/13 (broccoli) could lead to more patents being granted by the epo in respect of natural traits introduced into new varieties by means of essentially biological processes such as crossing and selection.
in writing. an ongoing wave of political and potentially ethnic violence has claimed 600 lives since the start of the year, with another 220,000 forced from their homes. the eu has allocated an additional eur 4.5 million to support these people. this resolution urges the government of burundi and the responsible authorities to put an immediate end to the violence and to stabilise the political and security situation. as a social democrat, i am glad that the resolution did not fail to recall the responsibility of the ruling powers to respect human and civil rights, which according to all available information are being grossly violated, there are persecutions, torture, even extrajudicial executions. the international community must take the situation in burundi seriously, as the escalation of the conflict and the resulting migration crisis could have huge negative impacts on the entire region.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution as i am deeply concerned by the grave security and political situation in burundi, the rapidly worsening humanitarian situation and the consequences that this may have for security and stability in the entire sub-region. by voting for this text i call for an immediate end to violence, human rights violations and political intimidation of opponents, and for the immediate disarmament of all armed groups allied to political parties, in strict accordance with international law and human rights. in this respect i urge all parties to establish the necessary conditions for rebuilding trust and fostering national unity, and call for the immediate resumption of an inclusive and transparent national dialogue.
in writing. ‒ i am sorry about the situation in the congo, but declarations from the european union will not solve anything.
in writing. ‒ i am deeply convinced of the importance of rapid international action to protect congo's virunga national park. this park bordering rwanda and uganda has many "neighbors": it is the oldest national park in africa, it is the most biologically diverse park in africa, but it is also the most threatened, especially by oil drilling plans and criminal activities of various armed groups associated with illegal logging, oil and poaching. these illegal activities finance not only armed rebel groups but also the official military forces. i believe it is absolutely necessary and in the best interest of all of us to prevent the destruction of this piece of land. its devastation would mean not only the loss of a unique and ecologically extremely important habitat and the loss of thousands of unique animal species, but also a social catastrophe, mass poverty in an already fractured state, an increase in extremism and regional instability. we have to stop all this.
in writing. - i am very pleased to have been able to support the european parliament resolution on the protection of the virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo. virunga national park is the most biologically diverse nature park in africa, and was inscribed on the unesco world heritage list in 1979. among other rare species, it is home to the endangered mountain gorilla. the resolution draws attention to the threat of irreversible damage to this national park as a result of oil exploration carried out by the british oil company soco international in violation of international conventions. in recent years, the park has become one of the most dangerous places in the world for wildlife conservation. in the last decade, over 140 park rangers have been killed on active duty. the park is the site of illegal exploitation of natural resources by armed groups linked to mining, who are also involved in large-scale poaching and use the proceeds to finance conflicts other than their own. i consider it necessary to draw attention to this threat and to call on the competent authorities to take measures to prevent illegal interference in the world's protected areas, which in turn leads to social unrest and even bloody conflicts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text on the protection of virunga national park in the drc. the text stresses the absolute need to prevent irreversible damage to the vnp, which was designated by unesco as a world heritage site in 1979 and as a world heritage site in danger in 1994. it also deplores the fact that the vnp has become one of the most dangerous places in the world when it comes to wildlife conservation and that armed groups have been involved in illegal exploitation of the park’s natural resources through mining activities and charcoal production used both to sustain their military operations and for personal gain. the text also urges the drc government to disarm rebels and restore security in the park region and regrets, furthermore, that the repression of human rights activists and journalists in the drc has increased. it calls once more on the drc government to recognise and respect freedom of the press and media and to uphold the rule of law and human rights.
